# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by crates/ripr/tests/cli_reference_doc.rs. Do not edit by hand;
     run `RIPR_BLESS_CLI_REFERENCE=1 cargo test -p ripr --test cli_reference_doc`. -->

Every `ripr` command and option, copied from the binary's own help. For a
guided start, read the [Quickstart](QUICKSTART.md). For exit codes, see
[EXIT_CODES.md](EXIT_CODES.md). In a terminal, `ripr help <command>` prints the
same text for one command and `ripr help --json` prints the machine-readable
catalog.

## Overview

```text
ripr — find changed code where nearby tests may not actually catch the
       changed behavior (Rust; Python and TypeScript in preview).

Usage:
  ripr <command> [options]

Try this first:
  ripr check                      Analyze the current diff, name the top gap.

Uses tracked edits, or committed history when clean. On a clean base branch,
edit a tracked source file first; new files need git add -N PATH.

The loop is: ripr names one gap -> you add one focused test -> ripr records
whether the gap closed. Commit your source change first, so `ripr repair` can
tell your new test apart from it. `ripr.toml` is optional; the zero-config run
is the intended first interface.

What are you trying to do?
  Diagnose setup        ripr doctor
  Inspect one change    ripr check [--base REV | --diff PATH]
                                   [--format human-full | json]
  Guided repo adoption  ripr pilot --root .
  Understand a finding  ripr explain <finding-id>
                        ripr context --at <finding-id>
  Repair a Rust gap     ripr repair [<item>]
                        # edit one focused test
                        ripr continue
  Repair a diff gap     follow the start from ripr check, when offered
  Compose PR evidence   ripr first-pr --root . --base BASE --head HEAD
  Work in an editor     ripr lsp --stdio (started by your editor)
  Adopt advisory CI     ripr init --ci github
  Wire up your agent    ripr init --agents all   (docs/AGENT_QUICKSTART.md)

More:
  ripr help <command>    Options for one command.
  ripr help --all        Every command, grouped by area.
  ripr help --json       Versioned machine-readable command catalog.

Exit codes: 0 completed, 2 could not complete (usage, configuration, or
operational error), 3 ripr declined: a blocking result, or a request it will
not run (the output says why), 130 interrupted standalone check. Full
contract: docs/EXIT_CODES.md.
Global flags: -v, --verbose   Extra pipeline diagnostics on stderr: analyzed
languages, mode, and counts (any position, except on `ripr help --json`).

ripr reads your changed code, imagines small bugs in it, and checks whether
your tests would likely catch them. It does not run mutants or your tests and
reports no runtime outcomes; a real mutation runner confirms later.
```

## Help text by command

### agent

`ripr help agent`

```text
Create a bounded repair transaction for a coding agent and inspect its evidence.

Usage: ripr agent <subcommand>

Primary workflow:
  repair    Run the before/edit/after repair transaction and its verification phase for one gap.
  status    Report existing agent-loop artifacts and the exact next command.

Advanced and compatibility workflows:
  start      Write a source-edit-free workflow manifest for one gap.
  brief      Rank the gaps in a working set so an agent starts at the strongest one.
  packet     Expand one visible gap into the existing agent gap packet JSON.
  card       Hand off one visible gap as the compact default repair card.
  stub       Write a compiling Rust test stub for one gap, ready to fill and run (Rust files only).
  verify     Compare before/after repo-exposure JSON for agent verification.
  verify-execute
             Run the one validated, bounded, read-only verify command that a packet names.
  receipt    Summarize one gap from agent verify JSON for review handoff.
  review-summary
             Join agent-loop artifacts into a compact review packet.

Repair path (start here):
  ripr repair [<item>]
  # edit one focused test
  ripr continue

The same transaction with explicit phases:
  ripr agent repair --seam-id ID --phase before
  # edit one focused test outside RIPR
  ripr agent repair --attempt ID --phase after

From a Rust `ripr check` finding, `ripr agent stub --at FILE:LINE` (the location
the finding prints) gives a ready-to-run test for that gap in one step. Stub
generation supports Rust files only; a Python or TypeScript path exits `3`.

`--seam-id` takes a repair ID from `ripr pilot --root .` or `ripr agent status`,
and `--phase before` also accepts a `ripr check` finding ID (`probe:...` or
`repo-probe:...`), a canonical gap ID, or a `file:line` location that names
one repair-eligible gap.

Run `ripr agent repair --help` for the primary repair workflow. Run
`ripr agent status --help` to inspect an interrupted or incomplete local loop.
The lower-level `start`, `brief`, `packet`, `verify`, `verify-execute`,
`receipt`, and `review-summary` help surfaces remain available for explicit
control, debugging, and compatibility.

Examples:
  ripr agent brief --root . --diff PATH --json
  ripr agent card --root . --seam-id ID
  ripr agent packet --root . --seam-id ID --json
  ripr agent repair --root . --seam-id ID --phase before
  ripr agent receipt --root . --verify-json agent-verify.json --seam-id ID --json
  ripr agent review-summary --root .
  ripr agent start --root . --seam-id ID
  ripr agent status --root .
  ripr agent stub --root . --at src/lib.rs:12
  ripr agent verify --root . --before before.json --after after.json --json
  ripr agent verify-execute --root . --packet packet.json --result-json result.json --authorize --json
```

### agent-brief

`ripr help agent brief`

```text
Write a bounded brief for a coding agent over the current diff or change.

Usage: ripr agent brief [--root PATH] (--diff PATH|--base REV|--files PATHS|--seam-id ID) --json [--max-seams N]

Options:
  --root PATH      Workspace root. Defaults to the current directory, then
                   walks up to the enclosing workspace or package, or the git
                   top level; `--root .` pins this directory.
  --diff PATH      Select a diff file and line-level working set. An existing
                   file typed relative to a member directory is bound to it.
                   The path must stay under --root; a diff outside it is
                   refused.
  --base REV       Derive the working set from a base revision.
  --files PATHS    Comma-separated repo-relative file paths; from a member
                   directory, existing files bind to that directory.
  --seam-id ID     Select one visible seam by ID.
  --json           Required until a human brief surface exists.
  --max-seams N    Requested seam cap. Defaults to 3 and cannot exceed 10.

When --files or --base produces a working set that matches no seams, the brief
falls back to all repo-actionable seams. This scope-widening is disclosed in
the warnings[] field of the JSON output — check warnings[] to confirm whether
you received a scoped result or a repo-wide fallback.

This parser is the agent-brief router's first implementation seam. The brief
router remains advisory and static; it does not run mutation testing, generate
tests, edit files, change cache behavior, or touch LSP/MCP surfaces.

Examples:
  ripr agent brief --root . --diff PATH --json
```

### agent-card

`ripr help agent card`

```text
Hand off one seam as the compact default repair card.

Usage: ripr agent card [--root PATH] --seam-id ID [--json]

Options:
  --root PATH      Workspace root. Defaults to the current directory, then
                   walks up to the enclosing workspace or package, or the git
                   top level; `--root .` pins this directory.
  --seam-id ID     Select one visible seam by ID, or by any ID that
                   `ripr check` or `ripr pilot` prints.
  --json           Emit the versioned repair_card.v1 JSON document. Without
                   this flag the same typed fields render as a short plain
                   brief; add the global `--verbose` for the full field list
                   (producer, subject, non-claim, detail routes).

The card command assembles the compact RepairCardV1 handoff for one seam: the
changed behavior, the exact blocker, the instruction state, the edit cage, the
done-when goals, and typed references to every omitted evidence family. The
complete canonical packet stays behind the card's explicit packet route
(`ripr agent packet --seam-id ID --json`), which remains the compatibility
path. It remains advisory and static; it does not run mutation testing,
generate tests, edit files, change cache behavior, or touch LSP/MCP surfaces.

Refusal contract: a deliberate named refusal — seam id not found,
policy-omitted seam, witness analysis unavailable, unnameable portable
workspace identity, or builder/budget refusal — exits `3`. Under `--json`
stdout carries one versioned `agent_card_refusal` envelope (`schema_version`
`0.1`) naming the typed `error.kind`, the asked-for `seam_id`, the verbatim
human prose, and one typed `remedy_route`, and stderr carries the prose
rendering; without `--json` stdout stays empty and stderr carries the prose
rendering only. Operational
failures (an unreadable config or a failed probe) stay exit `2` with human
prose only, like the sibling verify and repair commands.

Examples:
  ripr agent card --root . --seam-id ID
```

### agent-packet

`ripr help agent packet`

```text
Write a per-change handoff packet for a coding agent.

Usage: ripr agent packet [--root PATH] --seam-id ID --json
       ripr agent packet [--root PATH] --gap-ledger PATH --gap-id ID --json

Options:
  --root PATH        Workspace root. Defaults to the current directory, then
                     walks up to the enclosing workspace or package, or the git
                     top level; `--root .` pins this directory.
  --seam-id ID       Select one visible seam by ID, or by any ID that
                     `ripr check` or `ripr pilot` prints.
  --gap-ledger PATH  Explicit gap decision ledger JSON, read as typed from
                     the current directory.
  --gap-id ID        Select a GapRecord by gap_id or canonical_gap_id.
  --json             Required until a human packet surface exists.

The packet command expands a seam selected by `ripr agent brief` into the
existing agent-seam-packets-json envelope with one packet. With `--gap-ledger`,
it renders one agent packet from an explicit agent-packet-eligible GapRecord
without rerunning analysis. It remains advisory and static; it does not run
mutation testing, generate tests, edit files, change cache behavior, or touch
LSP/MCP surfaces.

A refusal (for example, an unknown seam or gap) exits `3` with the cause on
stderr and empty stdout.

Examples:
  ripr agent packet --root . --seam-id ID --json
```

### agent-receipt

`ripr help agent receipt`

```text
Write a provenance receipt with bounded next-action guidance for one change.

Usage: ripr agent receipt [--root PATH] --verify-json PATH --seam-id ID [--attempt ID] --json [--test NAME] [--command CMD] [--out PATH]

Options:
  --root PATH         Workspace root. Defaults to the current directory, then
                      walks up to the enclosing workspace or package, or the
                      git top level; `--root .` pins this directory.
  --verify-json PATH  JSON emitted by `ripr agent verify`. An existing file
                      typed relative to a member directory is bound to it.
  --seam-id ID        Select one seam from the verify JSON.
  --attempt ID        Bind the receipt to one repair attempt by id. Without
                      it the seam must have exactly one repair attempt; the
                      refusal names the ids found.
  --json              Required until a human receipt surface exists.
  --test NAME         Optional focused test added or changed by the agent.
  --command CMD       Optional verification command that was run. Repeatable.
  --out PATH          Write the JSON receipt to a file instead of stdout. A
                      relative path resolves against the resolved root, not
                      the current directory.

The receipt command narrows a saved agent verify artifact to one seam and adds
handoff metadata for review. The verify JSON path and the before/after snapshot
paths named inside it must resolve under `--root`; receipt provenance hashes
those three artifacts without rerunning analysis. With `--attempt`, the receipt
binds against that attempt's retained packet instead of the repository-global
compatibility packet a later attempt replaces. It remains advisory and
static; it does not run analysis, mutation testing, generate tests, edit files,
change cache behavior, or touch LSP/MCP surfaces.

Examples:
  ripr agent receipt --root . --verify-json agent-verify.json --seam-id ID --json
```

### agent-repair

`ripr help agent repair`

```text
Run the before/edit/after repair transaction and its verification phase for one named gap.

Usage: ripr agent repair [--root PATH] [--store PATH] --seam-id ID --phase before [--json]
       ripr agent repair [--root PATH] [--store PATH] --gap-id ID --base REF --phase before [--json]
       ripr agent repair [--root PATH] [--store PATH] (--attempt ID|--seam-id ID) --phase after [--json]
           [--test-result FILE]
       ripr agent repair [--root PATH] [--store PATH] --attempt ID --phase verify [--json]
           [--verify-authorized --verify-authority ID] [--verify-rollback]

Options:
  --root PATH          Workspace root. Defaults to the current directory, then
                       walks up to the enclosing workspace or package, or the git
                       top level; `--root .` pins this directory. A member-
                       relative `file:line` --seam-id is refused when a
                       workspace-root file with the same path suffix exists,
                       even without a root finding there; use `--root .` or
                       a seam or gap ID.
  --store PATH         Explicit repair-attempt store, resolved against --root.
                       Defaults to `target/ripr/repair-attempts`. Missing
                       explicit stores do not fall back to the default.
  --json               Print the phase's JSON document on stdout (the repair
                       packet, the after-phase result, or the verification
                       receipt). Without it stdout is a short summary and the
                       documents stay in their files under target/ripr/.
  --seam-id ID         Select one visible seam; required for `before` and the
                       compatibility selector for `after`. For `--phase before`,
                       a seam ID, a `ripr check` finding ID (`probe:` /
                       `repo-probe:`), a canonical gap ID, or a `file:line`
                       location naming exactly one repair-eligible seam
                       resolves to that seam. `--phase after` keeps exact seam
                       IDs. An unmapped ID refuses with the `ripr pilot`
                       recovery route.
  --gap-id ID          Start a repair for one canonical Python or TypeScript
                       preview gap printed by `ripr check`; exclusive with
                       `--seam-id` and requires `--base`. The before phase
                       re-runs the diff-scoped check, refuses unless the
                       finding's repair packet is ready, and records the
                       check-findings snapshot. Run
                       `--attempt ID --phase after` after committing the
                       focused test: it re-runs the check against the recorded
                       base commit, reports the gap closed only when it reads
                       exposed (otherwise it refuses and the attempt stays
                       retryable), then enforces the edit cage. It records
                       advisory static movement and an attempt receipt without
                       running the focused test. Run the suggested test command
                       and keep the repair only if that test passes.
  --base REF           The Git base the diff-scoped check compares against;
                       required with, and valid only for, `--gap-id`.
  --attempt ID         Select one durable repair attempt; valid for `after`
                       and `verify` (verify accepts only `--attempt`).
  --phase before|after|verify
                       Which phase of the repair loop to run. Defaults to
                       `before` (start a new attempt); `after` and `verify`
                       require an existing repair attempt.
  --python-repair-trust-manifest PATH
                       Bind this attempt to an accepted Python repair-trust
                       selection manifest; `before` only.
  --python-repair-trust-attempt ID
                       The selection attempt identity to bind; requires the
                       manifest flag.
  --edit-authorized    Explicitly authorize the bounded test-only edit for
                       this attempt; requires an authority.
  --edit-authority ID  The operator or agent identity the authorization is
                       recorded under; requires --edit-authorized.
  --verify-authorized  Explicitly authorize the bounded verification run for
                       this attempt; `verify` only; requires an authority.
  --verify-authority ID
                       The operator or agent identity the verification is
                       re-affirmed under (the same authority that authorized
                       the edit); requires --verify-authorized.
  --verify-rollback    After the observation, restore the applied edit and
                       record the rollback proof; `verify` only; requires the
                       verification authorization.
  --test-result FILE   A focused `cargo test` result you ran yourself, as a JSON
                       file with schema_version "0.1", kind
                       "focused_test_result", attempt_id, head, test_file and
                       libtest_events. `after` only. ripr does not run tests: it
                       checks that the result is bound to this attempt and the
                       current HEAD, names the selected test file, and has at
                       least one test that ran in that file or module, and that
                       no failure falls outside it and that the events it reports
                       close (every started test ends, every announced suite
                       finishes), then records the normalized result with the
                       attempt as a caller-reported claim.
                       Optional; it does not gate finish yet. Anything else is
                       refused and the attempt keeps waiting. Rust test files
                       only; save the file outside the checkout. A finish that
                       stops after the receipt evaluation began shows as
                       limited in status; start a new attempt.

The ordinary repair path is:

  ripr agent repair --seam-id ID --phase before
  # edit one focused test outside RIPR
  ripr agent repair --attempt ID --phase after

Use `--attempt ID` for the normal after phase. `--seam-id ID` remains a
compatibility route and fails closed when multiple awaiting attempts share a
seam.

The before phase writes the pre-edit repo-exposure snapshot and repair packet.
Without `--json`, stdout is a short summary ending with the exact next
command. With `--json`, it prints one JSON document: the packet envelope with
an additive `repair_attempt` block (attempt id, manifest path, packet path,
and the exact `--phase after` command), so a driver that captures only stdout
can complete the loop. The after phase writes the post-edit snapshot, persists
static verification JSON, and emits a receipt. RIPR owns the evidence
plumbing; the human or external agent owns the test edit.

With the Python repair-trust flags, the before phase verifies the selection
row by digest (manifest digest, row selection digest, current HEAD, exact
test-only target agreement with the packet) and stages the binding into the
durable attempt; the after phase re-verifies the same digests before recording
the applied edit and requires the same explicit authorization. A binding
drift, ambiguity, unsafe surface, or missing authorization fails before any
edit is recorded; repository HEAD drift between the phases is instead owned
by the durable finish, which records the typed stale state. The driver
records no verification result, no static movement, and no closure.

The verify phase (--attempt ID --phase verify --verify-authorized
--verify-authority ID) revalidates every retained identity of the applied
trust-bound attempt, executes only the packet's producer-owned typed verify
route through the bounded execution rails, reruns the analysis against the
exact post-edit state, compares the native-identity movement before/after,
optionally proves the rollback, and publishes one immutable candidate
receipt. Execution and static movement stay separate observations; the
receipt claims no lifecycle, acceptance, or closure state and no repair
correctness.

Lower-level `start`, `brief`, `packet`, `verify`, `receipt`, `status`, and
`review-summary` commands remain available for explicit control and debugging.
The repair command does not generate or apply tests, execute mutation testing,
or declare the repository safe to merge.

Repair scope: the edit target must match the test-surface path
convention (`tests`/`test` paths, `*_test`/`*_tests`, `test_*`, and
TypeScript test-file conventions). For external Rust test files, the cage
permits only insertion of new test functions and preserves existing test
bytes; an existing selected file must be committed before the start.
Other languages retain the whole-file path cage.
One exception: when a seam's only tests live in one inline `#[cfg(test)]`
module of the production file, the before phase can bind that module's
body as the edit cage instead — production code outside the module stays
untouched, and the file must be committed before the start.
Seams with no test-surface file and no such single inline module are out
of repair scope; the before phase refuses them before creating anything.

Environment variables:
  RIPR_PERSIST_LATENCY_TRACE  When present, emits diagnostic persist-phase
                                    trace lines for baseline capture, attempt
                                    publication, and after-phase state
                                    recapture. Presence enables tracing even
                                    if the value is empty or 0; it does not
                                    change any verdict.

A named refusal exits `3` with the cause on stderr; usage and operational
errors exit `2`.

Examples:
  ripr agent repair --root . --seam-id ID --phase before
```

`ripr help agent review-summary`

```text
Summarize agent-loop artifacts into a compact review packet.

Usage: ripr agent review-summary [--root PATH] [--json]

Options:

                   walks up to the enclosing workspace or package, or the git
                   top level; `--root .` pins this directory.
  --json           Emit the machine-readable review summary. Human Markdown is the default.

The review-summary command reads existing agent-loop artifacts and joins agent
status, receipt, workflow, operator cockpit, repo exposure, LSP cockpit when
present, and local CI artifact state into a compact review packet. It remains
advisory and static; it does not run analysis, mutation testing, generate
tests, edit files, change cache behavior, or touch LSP/MCP surfaces.

```

### agent-start

`ripr help agent start`

```text
Start a source-edit-free workflow packet for one selected change.

Usage: ripr agent start [--root PATH] --seam-id ID [--out PATH] [--json]

Options:
  --root PATH      Workspace root. Defaults to the current directory, then
                   walks up to the enclosing workspace or package, or the git
                   top level; `--root .` pins this directory.
  --seam-id ID     Select one visible seam by ID.
  --out PATH       Workflow output directory (relative to --root). Defaults to target/ripr/workflow.
  --json           Emit one machine-readable JSON document instead of the
                   `Wrote <path>` / `Next: <cmd>` prose lines:
                     {"schema_version": "0.1", "workflow": {"workflow_manifest": <path>,
                      "commands_markdown": <path>, "agent_brief": <path>},
                      "next_command": <cmd or null>}
                   Field names match the workflow manifest `outputs` block.

The start command writes a source-edit-free workflow packet for one seam:
workflow.json, commands.md, and agent-brief.json. The packet contains artifact
paths and shared command templates for the before snapshot, packet, brief,
after snapshot, verify, and receipt steps. It remains advisory and static; it
does not call an LLM API, run mutation testing, generate tests, edit files,
change cache behavior, or touch LSP/MCP surfaces.

A refusal (for example, an unknown seam or an unsupported language) exits `3`
with the cause on stderr.

Examples:
  ripr agent start --root . --seam-id ID
```

### agent-status

`ripr help agent status`

```text
Report local agent-loop artifact state and the next command to run.

Usage: ripr agent status [--root PATH] [--store PATH] [--attempt ID] [--json] [--out PATH]

Options:
  --root PATH      Workspace root. Defaults to the current directory, then
                   walks up to the enclosing workspace or package, or the git
                   top level; `--root .` pins this directory.
  --store PATH     Explicit repair-attempt store, resolved against --root.
                   Defaults to `target/ripr/repair-attempts`. Missing explicit
                   stores do not fall back to the default.
  --attempt ID     Select exactly one repair attempt by ID and report its
                   typed state, currentness posture, and one exact next or
                   recovery action. Without it, status lists every attempt in
                   the store and selects a next command only when that choice
                   is unambiguous; several active attempts are never resolved
                   by newest, first, same seam, or most recently modified. A
                   malformed or unbound attempt is reported as the typed
                   corrupt_or_unavailable result, never as another attempt's
                   state.
  --json           Emit the machine-readable status report. Human Markdown is the default.
  --out PATH       Must resolve to the default workflow directory
                   (target/ripr/workflow); any other path fails closed
                   because agent status reads only that directory.

Shell quoting: human Markdown states the host shell boundary in one line
before the emitted command; add the global `-v`/`--verbose` flag to restore
the full shell-quoting disclosure. Repeat polls in an agent loop therefore
stay small, and `--json` is unchanged (typed states, no prose).

The status command reads existing agent-loop artifacts under target/ripr only
and reports which before snapshot, after snapshot, brief, packet, verify, and
receipt files are present or missing. It may recover a seam_id from those
artifacts and emits the next command to run for missing inputs. It remains
advisory, static, and read-only; it does not run analysis, mutation testing,
generate tests, edit files, finish or restart repair attempts, change cache
behavior, or touch LSP/MCP surfaces.

Examples:
  ripr agent status --root .
```

### agent-stub

`ripr help agent stub`

```text
Write a compiling Rust test stub for one gap, ready to fill and run (Rust files only).

Usage: ripr agent stub [--root PATH] (--seam-id ID | --at FILE:LINE [--kind FAMILY]) [--write] [--json]

Options:
  --root PATH      Workspace root. Defaults to the current directory, then
                   walks up to the enclosing workspace or package, or the git
                   top level; `--root .` pins this directory.
  --seam-id ID     Select one visible seam by ID.
  --at FILE:LINE   Select the gap at a `ripr check` finding location.
  --kind FAMILY    With --at: the finding's probe family (`predicate`,
                   `return_value`, `error_path`, `match_arm`). Only seams of
                   that kind are tried, so a line holding several changes
                   stubs the one the finding reported; two separate seams of
                   that kind on one line are refused with their seam IDs.
                   `ripr check` prints it. Without it, --at tries only the
                   file's reported gaps, so a seam tests pin is refused.
  --write          Apply the stub: insert it into the owner file's inline
                   `#[cfg(test)]` module (or a new one), or create the
                   proposed `tests/` file. Refuses when the file changed
                   since the stub was computed or the new file exists. A
                   second --write for the same seam reports the stub already
                   written instead of suffixing a `_2` duplicate.
  --json           Emit one `rust_test_stub` JSON document (schema_version
                   `0.4`) with the placement, test name, exact text, the
                   `todo!()` fill-ins, derived inputs, run command, and
                   inventory `grip_class` plus check `classification`
                   when known. A strongly_gripped seam stays `state:
                   ready` (exit 0) and discloses the real reason in
                   `warnings` and human output: its tests already
                   discriminate it. When the seam's repair route is
                   established, the ready document also carries
                   `next_repair`: the `ripr agent repair --seam-id <id>`
                   start command, the repair packet's admitted edit
                   surface, and — when the stub's placement differs from
                   that surface — a `placement_divergence` naming both
                   files.

Stub generation supports Rust `.rs` paths only. Other --at paths receive
`unsupported_language` (exit `3`), including with --write. For a reported
gap, use the `ripr check` finding's test file/node and verify command when
available: edit the test by hand, run the native test command, then refresh
with `ripr check`. No stub is written for an unsupported language.

The stub calls the changed function with its real receiver and parameters,
fills a boundary input when the changed comparison names one, and stops at a
labelled `todo!()` for the value the behavior should produce. It compiles and
fails until that value is written; ripr never invents the expected value.
`--at --kind` still selects from that one file's seams without using
classification to pick the seam; after selection it looks up the inventory
grip so the stub can disclose it. A strongly_gripped seam is still a
scaffold (`state: ready`, exit 0): nothing is "configured off" — the seam is
exposed because existing tests already discriminate it, so the disclosure
says the stub is an optional scaffold, not evidence of a missing discriminator (only a class a user severity actually
disables is described as "configured off"). Side-effect and call-presence
gaps, async, unsafe, and generic owners are refused with a named reason
(exit `3`); under `--json` stdout
carries the `rust_test_stub` document with `state: refused` and stderr carries
the prose; without `--json` stdout stays empty on a refusal.

Examples:
  ripr agent stub --root . --at src/lib.rs:12
```

### agent-verify

`ripr help agent verify`

```text
Verify static-evidence movement between a before and after snapshot.

Usage: ripr agent verify [--root PATH] --before PATH --after PATH [--gap-id ID] --json

Options:
  --root PATH      Workspace root. Defaults to the current directory, then
                   walks up to the enclosing workspace or package, or the git
                   top level; `--root .` pins this directory.
  --before PATH    Before `repo-exposure-json` or `check-findings-json` snapshot.
  --after PATH     After snapshot of the same format.
  --gap-id ID      Bind the result to one canonical gap id (for example
                   `gap:typescript:typescript_preview:1a2b3c4d`) in two
                   `check-findings-json` snapshots. The gap must read open in
                   the before snapshot and `exposed` in the after snapshot;
                   absence from the after snapshot is never closure. Any other
                   outcome is a named refusal (exit `3`, empty stdout).
  --json           Required until a human verify surface exists.

The verify command compares two saved static artifacts (`repo-exposure-json`,
or `check-findings-json` for a diff-scoped TypeScript gap) and emits
an agent-focused before/after summary. Snapshot paths must resolve under
`--root`. The command remains advisory and static; it does not run analysis,
mutation testing, generate tests, edit files, change cache behavior, or touch
LSP/MCP surfaces.

Refusal contract: a typed verify refusal — drifted analysis inputs
(`analysis input identities differ`) or no repository movement between the
artifacts — names the cause on stderr, exits `3`, and leaves stdout empty
. Other rejections (unreadable or invalid artifacts, lineage
or metadata mismatches) exit `2`.

Movement vocabulary: the JSON output uses two related fields:
  - `change` (per-item): improved | changed | regressed | unchanged | new | resolved
  - `gap_movement` (per-item): closed | persisted | new
Precedence: `change: improved` means the grip class moved up; `gap_movement: closed`
means the gap disappeared entirely. A gap can persist even when grip improves.

The stdout document is the artifact `ripr agent receipt --verify-json` reads;
save it in the verify loop, for example:
  ripr agent verify --before before.repo-exposure.json --after after.repo-exposure.json --json > agent-verify.json

Examples:
  ripr agent verify --root . --before before.json --after after.json --json
```

### agent-verify-execute

`ripr help agent verify-execute`

```text
Execute one validated producer-owned verification route.

Usage: ripr agent verify-execute [--root PATH] --packet PATH --result-json PATH --authorize --json [--cancel-after-ms N]

Options:
  --root PATH          Workspace root. Defaults to the current directory, then
                       walks up to the enclosing workspace or package, or the
                       git top level; `--root .` pins this directory.
  --packet PATH        One producer-emitted agent packet JSON under --root. An
                       existing file typed relative to a member directory is
                       bound to it.
  --result-json PATH   New result path under --root; existing files are
                       refused. A relative path resolves against the resolved
                       root, not the current directory.
  --authorize          Required explicit authorization for process execution.
  --cancel-after-ms N  Optional operator deadline: kill the verify process N
                       milliseconds after it starts, before the packet's own
                       timeout. A hit is a bounded observation, not an error:
                       the result records the `cancelled` disposition and the
                       exit status stays 0.
  --json               Required machine-readable output.

Only the exact direct, no-network, no-write `ripr agent verify` route is
executable. Authority is layered: the packet's typed `command_specs.verify` must
be reproducible from its own `verification_commands`, so the route you read is
the route that runs; and both `--before` and `--after` must pass repo-exposure
provenance validation, after which the canonical route is recomputed from those
validated artifacts and must match the packet. The packet chooses which
producer artifacts to compare; it never authors the command.

The command uses the current ripr binary, a bounded timeout, output caps, and
repository currentness checks. The child environment is reduced to a disclosed
platform floor (PATH plus platform essentials); ambient credentials are dropped,
though HOME is passed through so host Git configuration still applies. Only the
owned child is terminated.

Every parsed attempt, including refusals, emits typed JSON on stdout; usage
errors stay on stderr. Exit status is 0 when a bounded observation was committed
-- including an observed command failure -- 3 for a typed refusal, and 2 when
the result could not be written. It
records process evidence only; it does not issue receipts, run mutation testing,
prove adequacy, or grant gate or merge authority.

Examples:
  ripr agent verify-execute --root . --packet packet.json --result-json result.json --authorize --json
```

### assistant-loop

`ripr help assistant-loop`

```text
Produce or summarize advisory agent proof and proof-loop health.

Usage:
  ripr assistant-loop proof [--pr-guidance PATH] [--agent-packet PATH] [--before PATH] [--after PATH] [--receipt PATH] [--ledger PATH] [--coverage-frontier PATH] [--gate-decision PATH] [--out PATH] [--out-md PATH]
  ripr assistant-loop health --proof PATH [--proof PATH ...] [--out PATH] [--out-md PATH]

Proof options:
  --root PATH                 Workspace root label. Defaults to current directory.
  --pr-guidance PATH          Optional PR guidance JSON from `ripr review-comments`.
  --agent-packet PATH         Optional editor/agent handoff JSON from `ripr agent brief`.
  --before PATH               Optional before repo-exposure JSON snapshot.
  --after PATH                Optional after repo-exposure JSON snapshot.
  --receipt PATH              Optional agent receipt JSON from `ripr agent receipt`.
  --ledger PATH               Optional PR evidence ledger JSON from `ripr pr-ledger record`.
  --coverage-frontier PATH    Optional coverage/grip frontier JSON.
  --gate-decision PATH        Optional gate-decision JSON from `ripr gate evaluate`.
  --out PATH                  JSON output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/test-oracle-assistant-proof.json.
  --out-md PATH               Markdown output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/test-oracle-assistant-proof.md.

The assistant-loop proof report is read-only advisory evidence over explicit
Campaign 20 artifacts. It requires at least one supplied artifact input, joins
PR guidance, agent handoff packets, before and after static evidence, receipts,
and optional CI projection artifacts, and marks missing proof pieces as
incomplete or unknown. It does not rerun analysis, post comments, edit source,
generate tests, call a provider, run mutation testing, change gate policy, or
make CI blocking by default.

Health options:
  --root PATH                 Workspace root label. Defaults to current directory.
  --proof PATH                Explicit test-oracle assistant proof JSON. Repeatable.
  --out PATH                  JSON output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/assistant-loop-health.json.
  --out-md PATH               Markdown output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/assistant-loop-health.md.

The assistant-loop health report is read-only advisory evidence over explicit
test-oracle assistant proof JSON artifacts. It summarizes proof completeness,
missing inputs, static movement, recurring warnings, and bounded repair queues.
It does not rerun analysis, inspect source to infer missing data, edit source,
generate tests, call a provider, run mutation testing, change gate policy, or
make CI blocking by default.

Examples:
  ripr assistant-loop health --proof target/ripr/reports/test-oracle-assistant-proof.json
  ripr assistant-loop proof --pr-guidance target/ripr/review/comments.json --agent-packet target/ripr/workflow/agent-brief.json --before target/ripr/pilot/repo-exposure.json --after target/ripr/pilot/after.repo-exposure.json --receipt target/ripr/reports/agent-receipt.json
```

### baseline

`ripr help baseline`

```text
Create, diff, and shrink a reviewed baseline of acknowledged test gaps.

Usage:
  ripr baseline create (--from PATH | --from-check PATH) [--out PATH] [--dry-run] [--force]
  ripr baseline diff --baseline PATH --current PATH [--out PATH] [--out-md PATH]
  ripr baseline update --baseline PATH --current PATH --remove-resolved [--migrate-legacy-identities] [--out PATH]
  ripr baseline update --baseline PATH --current PATH --migrate-legacy-identities [--out PATH]

Create options:
  --from PATH    Gate-decision JSON from `ripr gate evaluate`.
  --from-check PATH
                 Whole-repository `ripr check --format json` artifact, from
                 `ripr check --candidate-tree $(git rev-parse HEAD^{tree})`. Baselines the gap
                 classes weakly_exposed, reachable_unrevealed and no_static_path
                 of the entire tree. Refuses a diff-scoped or incomplete artifact.
                 Give exactly one of --from or --from-check.
  --out PATH     Baseline ledger path. Defaults to .ripr/gate-baseline.json.
  --dry-run      Print the baseline ledger JSON without writing.
  --force        Overwrite an existing baseline ledger.

Diff options:
  --baseline PATH    Required. Reviewed baseline ledger, for example .ripr/gate-baseline.json.
  --current PATH     Current gate-decision JSON from `ripr gate evaluate`.
  --out PATH         JSON output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/baseline-debt-delta.json.
  --out-md PATH      Markdown output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/baseline-debt-delta.md.

Update options:
  --baseline PATH               Reviewed baseline ledger to refresh.
  --current PATH                Current gate-decision JSON from `ripr gate evaluate`.
  --remove-resolved             Shrink-only mode; remove identities absent from current evidence.
  --migrate-legacy-identities   Replace reviewed legacy fallback identities with the
                                unambiguously joined current canonical gap id. One of
                                --remove-resolved or --migrate-legacy-identities is
                                required; adopting new debt is never supported.
  --out PATH                    Updated baseline path. Defaults to --baseline.

The baseline create command writes a stable reviewed historical-debt ledger
from existing gate-decision evidence. It includes advisory, acknowledged, and
blocking identities; skips suppressed, configured-off, not-applicable, and
malformed decisions; and refuses to overwrite by default. It does not edit
source, run analysis, run mutation testing, generate tests, change gate policy,
or make CI blocking by default.

The baseline diff command compares a reviewed baseline ledger with current
gate-decision evidence and writes advisory JSON/Markdown debt movement. It
reports still-present, resolved, new policy-eligible, acknowledged, suppressed,
stale, invalid, and missing-input identities. It does not update baselines,
edit source, run analysis, run mutation testing, generate tests, change gate
policy, or make CI blocking by default.

The baseline update command refreshes a reviewed baseline ledger.
`--remove-resolved` enables shrink-only removal of reviewed identities that
are absent from the current gate-decision evidence; without it, unmatched
entries are preserved with a warning, so a migration-only run never shrinks
the reviewed baseline. Malformed, ambiguous, canonically diverged, and
cross-root entries are always preserved for manual review, and new current
debt is never adopted. `--migrate-legacy-identities` deterministically
replaces a reviewed legacy `path:line:static_class` identity with the
unambiguously joined current canonical gap id, records each replacement under
the `update` section for independent review, and refuses cross-root or
conflicting migrations. Generated CI should not use
this command to rewrite checked-in baselines automatically.

Output discipline: report-producing subcommands write their JSON or Markdown
files and print human `Wrote ...` status lines to stdout. `baseline create
--dry-run` is the exception: it prints the candidate JSON to stdout without
writing a file.

Examples:
  ripr baseline create --from target/ripr/reports/gate-decision.json
  ripr baseline diff --baseline .ripr/gate-baseline.json --current target/ripr/reports/gate-decision.json
  ripr baseline update --baseline .ripr/gate-baseline.json --current target/ripr/reports/gate-decision.json --remove-resolved
```

```text
                                --remove-resolved or --migrate-legacy-identities is
                                required; adopting new debt is never supported.
  --out PATH                    Updated baseline path. Defaults to --baseline.

The baseline update command refreshes a reviewed baseline ledger.
`--remove-resolved` enables shrink-only removal of reviewed identities that
are absent from the current gate-decision evidence; without it, unmatched
entries are preserved with a warning, so a migration-only run never shrinks
the reviewed baseline. Malformed, ambiguous, canonically diverged, and
cross-root entries are always preserved for manual review, and new current
debt is never adopted. `--migrate-legacy-identities` deterministically
replaces a reviewed legacy `path:line:static_class` identity with the
unambiguously joined current canonical gap id, records each replacement under
the `update` section for independent review, and refuses cross-root or
conflicting migrations. Generated CI should not use
this command to rewrite checked-in baselines automatically.

Output discipline: report-producing subcommands write their JSON or Markdown
files and print human `Wrote ...` status lines to stdout. `baseline create
--dry-run` is the exception: it prints the candidate JSON to stdout without
writing a file.

Examples:
  ripr baseline update --baseline .ripr/gate-baseline.json --current target/ripr/reports/gate-decision.json --remove-resolved

Run `ripr help baseline` for every baseline subcommand.
```

### cache

`ripr help cache`

```text
Inspect, export or clear the disposable analysis cache.

Usage:
  ripr cache status [--root PATH] [--json]
  ripr cache export [--root PATH] --out NEW_DIRECTORY
  ripr cache clear [--root PATH] [--dry-run] [--force]

Examples:
  ripr cache status --json
  ripr cache export --out NEW_DIRECTORY
  ripr cache clear --dry-run
```

### cache-clear

`ripr help cache clear`

```text
Evict ripr cache entries.

Usage: ripr cache clear [--root PATH] [--dry-run] [--force]

Removes only recognized ripr cache layers under the resolved cache directory
(RIPR_CACHE_DIR when set, otherwise target/ripr/cache under the Cargo workspace
root). The cache root and unrelated sibling files or directories are preserved.

  --root PATH Analyzed root, as passed to `ripr check --root PATH`. Selects
              <PATH>/target/ripr/cache regardless of the current directory.
              RIPR_CACHE_DIR still wins when set.
  --dry-run   Report what would be removed and remove nothing.
  --force     Required to remove cache layers that hold entries.

Examples:
  ripr cache clear --dry-run
```

### cache-export

`ripr help cache export`

```text
Copy a validated current-input cache snapshot without historical generations.

Usage: ripr cache export [--root PATH] --out NEW_DIRECTORY

Copy a qualified current-input cache snapshot, excluding historical keys,
unreferenced shards, fingerprint mappings and staging files. The live cache
is never changed. Run repo exposure or repo badge analysis first.

  --root PATH   Analyzed root, preserving the spelling supplied to check.
                Default: the same implicit workspace resolution as check.
  --out PATH    New cache directory; its parent must already exist.

Success prints JSON with entry counts and logical_file_bytes (encoded file
lengths, not allocated filesystem bytes). Restore the completed directory as
RIPR_CACHE_DIR for the same workspace path, analyzer build and input identity.
Missing optional file facts are counted; corrupt present entries refuse export.
Require exit zero before using or publishing the output. On failure, incomplete
owned output is retained and named. Existing destinations, cache overlap and
linked paths are refused. Concurrent hostile directory replacement is outside
this cooperative-filesystem contract. No live-cache history is deleted.

Examples:
  ripr cache export --out NEW_DIRECTORY
```

### cache-status

`ripr help cache status`

```text
Show cache occupancy and entry health.

Usage: ripr cache status [--root PATH] [--json]

Report the resolved analysis cache directory (RIPR_CACHE_DIR when set,
otherwise target/ripr/cache under the Cargo workspace root).

  --root PATH   Analyzed root, as passed to `ripr check --root PATH`. Selects
                <PATH>/target/ripr/cache regardless of the current directory.
                RIPR_CACHE_DIR still wins when set. Default: the workspace
                root resolved from the current directory.
  --json    Print machine-readable status JSON. Its `schema_version` is the
            version of this status report, not of the on-disk cache layers
            (those carry their own version in their directory names).

`entry_count` and `total_size_bytes` count only the recognized ripr cache
layer directories, the same set `ripr cache clear` removes; files anywhere
else under the cache root — including a regular file wearing a layer name —
are reported separately as unrecognized entries and are always preserved by
clear. A cache path reached through a symlink or junction (leaf or ancestor)
is resolved to the real directory (via_symlink/real_cache_dir), matching
what `ripr check` reads and writes.

The cache is disposable: deleting it only costs a slower next run. Use
`ripr cache clear` to remove it.

Examples:
  ripr cache status --json
```

### calibrate

Shared help for `ripr calibrate`, `ripr calibrate cargo-mutants`.

```text
Import cargo-mutants outcomes as advisory calibration over static evidence.

Usage: ripr calibrate cargo-mutants --mutants-json PATH --repo-exposure-json PATH [--format md|markdown|text|json] [--out PATH]

Options:
  --mutants-json PATH          cargo-mutants JSON file, or mutants.out directory containing outcomes.json and/or mutants.json. A mutants.json-only import counts unexecuted candidates in matched_total.
  --repo-exposure-json PATH    RIPR repo-exposure-json snapshot to join against.
  --format FORMAT             md, markdown, text, or json. Defaults to md.
  --out PATH                  Write the rendered calibration report to a file instead of stdout.

The calibration report is advisory. It imports already-produced runtime
mutation data and joins it to static seam evidence by seam_id first, then by
the unique innermost seam span that contains the mutant's span, then by
unambiguous file/line where no span decides. Equal or crossing spans stay
ambiguous. It does not run mutation testing, alter static classifications, or
configure CI policy.

Producing the input:
  Install cargo-mutants (`cargo install cargo-mutants --locked`) and run
  `cargo mutants` so it writes `mutants.out/`. Pass that directory,
  `mutants.out/outcomes.json`, or `mutants.out/mutants.json`. A
  mutants.json-only path counts unexecuted candidates in matched_total;
  those rows have no runtime observation and render as unknown /
  no_runtime_data. Pass outcomes.json, or a mutants.out directory that
  includes it, when the Summary counts should reflect observed runtime
  evidence. cargo-mutants selection flags only narrow its own run; ripr
  does not invoke it. The importer was validated against cargo-mutants
  27.1.0 `outcomes.json` and `mutants.json` shapes. A checked-in example
  ships in the ripr repository's calibration fixtures
  (runtime-mutants.json).

Limitation: the join matches by seam_id, span containment, or file/line. It
does not check that the cargo-mutants JSON and the repo-exposure snapshot
describe the same repository or commit. cargo-mutants outcomes.json does not carry a head SHA.
When the snapshot carries a head, ripr names that subject on stderr and in
the report's Provenance section (md) or provenance.disclosure field (JSON), so an
artifact saved with --out keeps the same caveat; when either artifact lacks
a head, ripr says so and asks you to ensure both artifacts are from the
same repository and adjacent commits. Matching heads still do not mean
matching working trees. A coincidental file:line from another subject can
still join, including with a high-signal confidence label.

Examples:
  ripr calibrate cargo-mutants --mutants-json PATH --repo-exposure-json PATH
```

### capabilities

`ripr help capabilities`

```text
Show what ripr can establish per language, framework and mode.

Usage: ripr capabilities [--language NAME] [--json | --markdown]

Options:
  --language NAME  Narrow to one language: rust, typescript, javascript,
                   python or perl.
  --json           Emit the versioned machine-readable registry.
  --markdown       Emit the generated registry block for
                   docs/status/SUPPORT_TIERS.md (whole table; not with
                   --json or --language).

The default screen is one plain sentence per language. `--json` and
`--markdown` carry the full table: each cell names a language, framework, mode
(diff or repo) and family (static_facts or repair_routing) with one closed
support state, a tier ceiling, the limit or fallback to honor, and the specs
that define the claim. A combination with no cell is not_proven.

This is a static registry for this build. Adapter availability (compiled or
not) is reported separately and never changes a cell. It does not say whether
a language is enabled for a repository; use `ripr doctor` for that. It reads
no repository, runs nothing and promotes no support tier.

Examples:
  ripr capabilities --json
```

### check

`ripr help check`

```text
Analyze the current diff and name the changed behavior your tests may not catch.

Usage: ripr check [OPTIONS] [PATH...]

Common options:
  --base REV        Compare against this revision; when omitted, ripr uses
                    the origin/HEAD ref, then origin/main, origin/master, main, master.
  --diff PATH       Read a diff file instead of running git diff (`-` = stdin).
  --worktree        Include staged and unstaged tracked edits (already the
                    default when the tree has them).
  --committed       Compare committed history only (base...HEAD).
  --format FORMAT   human (default); human-full lists every finding with
                    drill-in commands; json (or --json) for scripts and CI;
                    json-compact keeps the same JSON with less whitespace;
                    agent gives compact triage; github/sarif for annotations.
  --mode MODE       instant, draft (default), fast, deep, or ready: how much
                    of the workspace is indexed (never changes a class).
  --root PATH       Workspace root. Defaults to the current directory, then
                    walks up to the enclosing workspace or package, or the git
                    top level (never past the repository); `--root .` pins
                    this directory.
  --quiet           Suppress stderr progress; known seam totals as processed_n_of_total.
                    Unknown totals show no percentage or ETA, and progress makes no speed claim.
  --timeout SECS    Analysis-worker budget (600s default; 0 off; repo formats skip).
                    Pre-worker git/post-run rendering outside; in-worker git diff
                    load counts against it (each git call has its own timeout). Raise/disable on analysis_timeout.
Exit status: 0 for a completed run, including findings that are `exposed` or weak.
`unsupported_input` reports exit 2, as do usage errors. Do not build
a CI gate on check's exit code; run `ripr gate evaluate` (exit 3 on `blocked`).
Examples:
  ripr check [src/lib.rs]   (a PATH keeps only that changed file, like --path)
  ripr check --base origin/main --json --quiet   (--json on a pipe is already quiet; --quiet also silences a terminal)
More:
  ripr check --help --all   Every option (--path/--exclude too), format, and env var.
```

Every option: `ripr help check --all`

```text
Analyze a diff or workspace and emit findings in human, JSON, SARIF, or badge form.

Usage: ripr check [OPTIONS] [PATH...]

Options:
  --root PATH              Workspace root. Defaults to current directory, then
                           walks up to a Cargo.toml containing [workspace];
                           without one, to the nearest Cargo.toml or the git
                           top level. The walk never leaves the git
                           repository. A moved root is disclosed on stderr.
                           When that move skips a closer ripr.toml, stderr
                           names both files and which one governed. Recovery
                           is `--root .` from that directory.
  --base REV               Base revision for git diff. When omitted, ripr uses
                           the local origin/HEAD ref, then origin/main,
                           origin/master, main, and master in order; when none
                           of those resolves, the analysis does not run. The
                           diff ends at HEAD on a clean tree and at the working
                           tree when it has uncommitted changes (see
                           --worktree and --committed); the human, JSON,
                           GitHub, and SARIF outputs name the base and head
                           that were analyzed.
  --diff PATH              Read a unified diff file instead of running git diff.
                           Use --diff - to read from stdin (e.g.
                           `git diff origin/main | ripr check --diff -`).
  --candidate-tree TREE    Analyze exactly this immutable Git tree object.
                           Derives the diff from Git objects alone; the
                           worktree and index are never consulted. Mutually
                           exclusive with --diff and --base.
  --candidate-base BASE    Base treeish for --candidate-tree (a commit, tag,
                           or tree OID). Defaults to the repository's empty
                           tree.
  --path GLOB              Analyze only changed files matching GLOB
                           (repeatable). A repository-relative file, directory
                           or glob: `src/lib.rs`, `crates/api`, `src/**/*.rs`.
                           Applied before the diff-size limits, so they measure
                           only the chosen files. Changed files outside the
                           scope are named in a language_scope_unsupported
                           limitation and have no finding: the outcome is
                           partial_with_limitations, never clean. A scope that
                           leaves no changed file is an error. Not supported
                           for repo-scoped formats. A bare PATH argument
                           (`ripr check src/lib.rs`) is the same as --path.
  --exclude GLOB           Skip changed files matching GLOB (repeatable;
                           wins over --path). Same pattern shapes, same
                           disclosure as --path.
  --worktree               Diff the base revision against the live working tree
                           instead of HEAD, including staged and unstaged
                           tracked edits. This is already the default when the
                           tree has staged or unstaged tracked edits;
                           untracked files never select it and stay out of
                           the diff until staged (`git add -N`).
                           Cannot be combined with --diff.
  --committed              Diff committed history only (base...HEAD) even when
                           the working tree has uncommitted changes; the
                           output then notes that those edits were not
                           analyzed. Cannot be combined with --worktree,
                           --diff, --candidate-tree, or repo-scope formats.
  --legend                 Print the Evidence stage and summary definitions in
                           the human output (a lookup: it does not record the
                           first run). They are shown on the first run in a
                           build tree; later runs keep one pointer line. No
                           effect on other formats.
  --mode MODE              How much of the workspace is indexed: instant
                           (changed files only, cheapest), draft (packages the
                           diff touches; the default), fast (same as draft for
                           now), deep and ready (whole workspace, slowest).
                           Modes never change what an exposure class means.
                           Cost class: whole-workspace modes (deep, ready) can
                           take roughly an order of magnitude longer than the
                           diff-scoped modes (instant, draft, fast) on large
                           workspaces. See docs/CONFIGURATION.md "Analysis
                           modes".
  --format FORMAT          Output format. Defaults to human.
                           Choose by task: eye review -> human (the default);
                           every finding with drill-in commands -> human-full;
                           machine consumer (jq, CI scripts) -> json (--json);
                           same document with less whitespace for a machine
                           or coding agent -> json-compact;
                           same findings with repeated evidence prose coded
                           against a document-head legend -> json-terse;
                           compact report for a coding agent -> agent;
                           one sorted path:line:col gap line per actionable
                           finding, nothing for exposed -> missed-txt;
                           file annotations in Actions logs -> github; code
                           scanning upload -> sarif (bounded minified:
                           sarif-compact); README badge ->
                           repo-badge-shields (repo ledger); PR/CI status
                           badge -> badge-shields (diff); whole-repo
                           inventory -> repo-exposure-json; agent repair
                           evidence -> agent-seam-packets-json. Groups:
                             Analysis (diff-scoped):
                               human, human-full, json, json-compact,
                               json-terse, github,
                               sarif, sarif-compact, agent, missed-txt,
                               check-findings-json (identified snapshot
                               for `agent verify`)
                             Badge (diff-scoped, for PR/CI status):
                               badge-json, badge-shields,
                               badge-plus-json, badge-plus-shields
                             Repo-scope (full-repo analysis):
                               repo-seams-json, repo-seams-md,
                               repo-exposure-json, repo-exposure-summary-json,
                               repo-exposure-md, repo-sarif, repo-sarif-compact,
                               repo-badge-json, repo-badge-shields,
                               repo-badge-plus-json, repo-badge-plus-shields
                             Agent (machine-readable repair evidence):
                               agent-seam-packets-json
                           missed-txt prints `path:line:col: <classification>
                           <probe family>: <expression> -> <missing
                           discriminator>` for each candidate-actionable,
                           unsuppressed, non-exposed finding, sorted; exposed
                           findings print nothing. Static classification only;
                           no runtime mutation outcome is claimed.
                           json-compact is the same check document as json,
                           with only insignificant whitespace removed and one
                           final newline. Evidence, source identity, actions,
                           limitations, refusal documents and exit codes stay
                           unchanged. It uses the same pre-compaction findings
                           budget, not extra findings bought by smaller output.
                           It is not the summarized agent format or the
                           identified check-findings-json verification artifact.
                           badge-plus-* and repo-badge-plus-* formats read
                           target/ripr/reports/test-efficiency.json when present;
                           missing input renders a neutral "needs test-efficiency"
                           badge and warns on stderr. No public ripr command
                           writes that file yet; hand-author the documented
                           minimum shape from real test measurements or wait
                           for the portable producer (not shipped yet).
                           See docs/BADGE_ADOPTION.md.
                           repo-* and agent-seam-packets-json formats render
                           against the full repo baseline; the non-repo badge-*
                           formats remain diff-scoped.
  --gap-ledger PATH        For repo-badge-* formats only, render badge counts
                           from explicit gap-decision-ledger projection targets
                           instead of seam-native/test-efficiency counts.
  --json                   Shortcut for --format json.
  --no-unchanged-tests     Limit the index to changed Rust files.
  --perl-facts PATH        Use the explicit Perl facts packet as the
                           analysis input for Perl files.
  --suppression-policy PATH
                           Apply a suppressions TOML (same schema as
                           .ripr/suppressions.toml) to the findings-based
                           formats (human, human-full, json, json-compact,
                           github, missed-txt). exposure_gap
                           entries select findings by finding_id or by a
                           path glob (with optional static_class narrowing).
                           Suppressed findings stay visible in JSON with
                           suppressed: true; per-class summary counts cover
                           unsuppressed findings only. Relative PATH
                           resolves against --root; a missing or malformed
                           policy fails the run.
  --output-dir DIR         With a named --diff file, write native badge.json,
                           detail.json and human.txt from one analysis. DIR must
                           be new (parent exists). Verify manifest.json and member
                           hashes before consuming the set. Does not combine with
                           --format/--json, scope switches, --gap-ledger,
                           --write-artifact or --suppression-policy. Bounded input
                           inventory refuses drift, nonregular files and external
                           module reads. See docs/OUTPUT_SCHEMA.md.
  --write-artifact PATH    Write a full-fidelity check artifact (schema
                           ripr-check-artifact-v1) for later
                           `ripr explain --from PATH` /
                           `ripr context --from PATH` reuse. The artifact
                           records the complete finding set plus the input
                           identity (diff bytes hash, root, mode, languages,
                           analysis options, config identity, analyzer
                           version). It is a local, disposable derivative:
                           never a gate, badge, or proof input. Diff-scoped
                           findings runs only, including --worktree runs
                           (the recorded base-to-worktree diff is re-resolved
                           at reuse time; a changed worktree is refused by the
                           diff bytes hash); not supported for repo-scoped
                           formats, --gap-ledger, or managed [perl] producer
                           packet generation (pass --perl-facts PATH
                           explicitly instead).
                           Stdin (--diff -) is not supported: save stdin to
                           a named diff file and pass --diff PATH instead.
  --git-timeout SECS       Cooperative deadline in seconds for each git
                           invocation in the diff-load path. A git command
                           that exceeds the deadline is terminated and the
                           error names git_invocation_timeout. 0 disables
                           the deadline. Default: 300 (5 minutes). Also
                           settable via RIPR_GIT_TIMEOUT env var.
  --timeout SECS           Analysis-worker wall-clock budget in seconds (not
                           the repo-wide repo-exposure and seam formats).
                           Pre-analysis git work and post-analysis rendering
                           are outside this budget; git-backed diff loading
                           inside the worker counts against it, and each git
                           invocation is bounded separately by RIPR_GIT_TIMEOUT.
                           When the analysis worker exceeds it, check stops and
                           refuses with analysis_timeout: no findings are
                           produced and the result is never a clean pass. 0
                           disables the budget. Default: 600 (10 minutes). Also
                           settable via RIPR_CHECK_TIMEOUT env var.
  --quiet                  Suppress analysis progress and heartbeats on
                           stderr. Does not change machine stdout, exit
                           codes, or error reporting.
  --all                    With --help: print this exhaustive reference
                           instead of the one-screen summary.

Exit status:
  Complete and partial_with_limitations reports exit 0, including findings
  that are `exposed` or weak. A non-zero exit means the analysis did not
  complete, not that it disapproved of the diff.
  `unsupported_input` reports exit 2 after the original report is written;
  limitations and recovery routes remain available in that report. Usage and
  operational errors also exit 2.
  Empty input is complete no_scope (exit 0). Read the outcome in the JSON to
  distinguish partial analysis from complete analysis; a successful exit
  alone does not establish complete scope or a clean gate. Blocking belongs
  to `ripr gate evaluate` (exit 3 on `blocked`). Do not build a CI gate on
  check's exit code; read its output, or run the gate.

Progress:
  Long-running check analysis writes producer stages to stderr as
  `ripr progress: <stage> [<scope>]` and, while a stage stays active,
  throttled `still active after <elapsed class>` heartbeats. When a
  repo-inventory walk has an honest seam denominator, those lines also
  carry `processed_<n>_of_<total>` so a multi-minute `repo-exposure-json`
  run can be told from a hang. Non-TTY / CI output is newline-delimited
  with no control sequences. A TTY may reuse one line and stays silent
  for sub-threshold flashes. Machine formats (json, json-compact, sarif,
  github, missed-txt) keep stdout byte-clean. With json, json-compact, sarif,
  missed-txt, badge-*
  or agent selected and stderr not a terminal, the stream is off by default;
  `RIPR_PROGRESS=1` restores it. A terminal and the human formats keep it. Unknown totals
  never become a percentage or ETA. Progress does not mean analysis is faster
  or that the command will succeed. `--quiet` turns this stream
  off; so does setting `RIPR_QUIET` to anything but empty, `0` or
  `false`. `repair` and `continue` accept `--quiet` too and drop their
  progress narration and `wrote <path>` lines; refusal prose is never
  suppressed.

Environment variables:
  RIPR_MAX_DIFF_CHANGED_LINES             Maximum added plus removed diff lines recorded
                                          while parsing a unified diff before check
                                          stops with diff_scope_oversized (language-
                                          neutral; per-language adapter limits may
                                          still apply). With --json, stdout carries a
                                          non-consumable limited artifact.
                                          Default: 100000.
  RIPR_MAX_DIFF_CHANGED_RUST_LINES        Maximum added plus removed Rust diff lines
                                          analyzed. A larger diff degrades into a
                                          limited_partial_scope partition; check
                                          stops with diff_scope_oversized only when
                                          no changed file fits within it. With
                                          --json, stdout carries a non-consumable
                                          limited artifact. Default: 2000.
  RIPR_MAX_DIFF_CHANGED_PYTHON_LINES      Maximum added plus removed Python diff
                                          lines analyzed (the Rust guard's memory
                                          bound for the Python adapter); degrades
                                          like the Rust limit. Default: 2000.
  RIPR_MAX_DIFF_CHANGED_TYPESCRIPT_LINES  Maximum added plus removed TypeScript
                                          diff lines (the routed .ts/.tsx/.mts/
                                          .cts/.js/.jsx/.mjs/.cjs family)
                                          analyzed; degrades like the Rust limit.
                                          Default: 2000.
  RIPR_MAX_DIFF_INDEX_FILES               Maximum Rust files loaded into the diff
                                          index before check stops with
                                          diff_scope_oversized (a memory guard).
                                          With --json, stdout carries a
                                          non-consumable limited artifact.
                                          Default: 10000.
  RIPR_DIFF_NARROW_INDEX_FILES            Index size above which Draft/Fast
                                          narrows dependent packages and stops
                                          widening reach searches. Bounds time,
                                          never refuses; clamped to
                                          RIPR_MAX_DIFF_INDEX_FILES. Default: 1200.
  RIPR_DIFF_DEPENDENT_SCOPE               How Draft/Fast indexes packages that
                                          depend on the changed ones: auto (whole
                                          while under RIPR_DIFF_NARROW_INDEX_FILES,
                                          else named), named (only files that can
                                          change a result), or full. Default: auto.
  RIPR_PARTIAL_DIFF_FILE_BUDGET           Changed-line files analyzed before check
                                          returns a bounded limited_partial_scope
                                          partition with exact selected paths,
                                          lower-bound uninspected counts, and a
                                          named stop reason; gate/baseline/badge/Zero
                                          ineligible. Overrides above the effective
                                          limit are clamped with disclosure. Invalid
                                          values are rejected as partial_budget_invalid.
                                          Default: 200.
  RIPR_PARTIAL_DIFF_LINE_BUDGET           Changed lines analyzed before check
                                          returns limited_partial_scope. The first
                                          selected file is always analyzed, even
                                          when it alone exceeds the budget.
                                          Overrides above the effective limit are
                                          clamped with disclosure. Invalid values
                                          are rejected as partial_budget_invalid.
                                          Default: 1000.
  RIPR_CHECK_FINDINGS_BYTES               Pre-compaction findings-array byte budget
                                          for json and json-compact. Retains the
                                          first finding even if it alone exceeds
                                          the budget; further findings may be
                                          omitted with full counts and an explicit
                                          limited_findings_bound disclosure.
                                          Compaction does not change membership.
                                          Set to 0 for unbounded findings;
                                          an unparseable value fails the run.
                                          Default: 1000000 (1 MB).
  RIPR_QUIET                              Silence the stderr `ripr progress:` stream
                                          like --quiet (check, explain, context,
                                          pilot, repair, continue). Any value except
                                          empty, 0 or false silences it; stdout, exit
                                          codes and errors are unchanged.
  RIPR_PROGRESS                           Keep the `ripr progress:` stream for a
                                          machine format on a non-terminal stderr,
                                          where it is off by default. Any value
                                          except empty, 0 or false restores it.
  RIPR_GIT_TIMEOUT                        Cooperative deadline in seconds for each
                                          git invocation in the diff-load path. A
                                          git command that exceeds the deadline is
                                          terminated and the error names
                                          git_invocation_timeout. 0 disables the
                                          deadline. Invalid values are rejected.
                                          Default: 300 (5 minutes).
  RIPR_REPO_EXPOSURE_LATENCY_TRACE        When present, emits diagnostic phase/cache
                                          trace lines for repo-exposure analysis.
                                          Presence enables tracing even if the value
                                          is empty or 0; it does not change the
                                          analysis verdict.
  RIPR_ALLOW_REPO_PERL_EXECUTABLE         Set to 1 to let [perl].executable from
                                          ripr.toml run as the Perl facts exporter.
                                          Unset, ripr ignores it and runs the
                                          exporter from PATH, so a cloned
                                          repository cannot choose a program for
                                          ripr to run.

Examples:
  ripr check
  ripr check --base HEAD~1
```
