```text
  ripr check --base HEAD --worktree
  ripr check --base origin/main --committed
  ripr check --base origin/main --format json-compact
  ripr check --diff crates/ripr/examples/sample/example.diff --format github
  ripr check --mode ready --json
  ripr check --base origin/main --json --suppression-policy policy/ripr-suppressions.toml
  ripr check --diff d.patch --write-artifact target/ripr/last-check.json
```

### completions

`ripr help completions`

```text
Print a tab-completion script for your shell.

Usage: ripr completions <bash|zsh|fish|powershell>

Options:
  --help  Show this help.

The script completes ripr command names and the word after a command, such as
`cache status`. It does not complete flags. It prints to stdout and changes
nothing on your machine.

Try it in the current shell:
  bash        source <(ripr completions bash)
  zsh         source <(ripr completions zsh)   (run `compinit` first)
  fish        ripr completions fish | source
  powershell  ripr completions powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression

To keep it, add that line to your shell startup file (for example ~/.bashrc,
~/.zshrc, ~/.config/fish/config.fish or your PowerShell profile).

Examples:
  ripr completions bash
```

### config

Shared help for `ripr config`, `ripr config validate`.

```text
Validate the repository's ripr.toml without running workspace probes.

Usage: ripr config validate [--root PATH]

Options:
  --root PATH  Starting root for ancestor config discovery. Defaults to `.`.

The command uses the same ancestor-aware loader as analysis and fails with the
path-qualified parser or policy error. A missing ripr.toml follows the normal
built-in-defaults path; use `ripr init` when you want to materialize those
defaults into a file.

Examples:
  ripr config validate --root PATH
```

### context

`ripr help context`

```text
Print one finding's changed code and related tests for an agent or script.

Use this when an agent or tool needs the facts behind one `ripr check`
finding: the changed expression ripr examined, the tests that appear to
reach it, the values they check, and any assertion that seems to be missing.
Output is always JSON. To read the same finding as prose, run `ripr explain`
with the same selector.

Usage: ripr context [--root PATH] [--base REV] [--worktree|--committed|--diff PATH] [--from PATH] [--path GLOB] [--exclude GLOB] [--mode MODE] [--no-unchanged-tests] [--perl-facts PATH] [--suppression-policy PATH] --at <finding-id|file:line> [--max-related-tests N] [--json] [--quiet]

Options:
  --at <finding-id|file:line>
               Required. The finding to describe: an id from
               `ripr check --json`, or a changed `file:line`.
  --finding ID
               Same as --at.
  --max-related-tests N
               List at most N related tests. Defaults to
               `reports.max_related_tests` in ripr.toml, otherwise 5.
  --root PATH  Workspace root. Defaults to the current directory, then
               walks up to the enclosing workspace or package, or the git
               top level; `--root .` pins this directory. A member-relative
               `file:line` selector binds to the directory you ran from like
               `ripr explain`; --diff and --from paths are read as typed from
               the current directory.
  --base REV   Compare against this revision, as in `ripr check --base`.
               Not combinable with --diff unless --from is also given.
  --diff PATH  Read a diff file instead of running git diff (`-` = stdin).
  --committed  Analyze committed history only (base...HEAD), even when the
               working tree is dirty. Not combinable with --worktree, --diff
               or --from. Without a supplied scope, dirty repositories use
               the same worktree default as `ripr check`.
  --worktree   Analyze staged and unstaged tracked edits, like
               `ripr check --worktree` (see `ripr explain --help`).
  --path GLOB  Analyze only changed files matching GLOB (repeatable). Same
               patterns and intake filter as `ripr check --path`. A scoped
               `ripr check` prints this flag on its context drill-in.
  --exclude GLOB
               Skip changed files matching GLOB (repeatable; wins over
               --path). Same patterns as `ripr check --exclude`.
  --from PATH  Load findings from a check artifact written by
               `ripr check --write-artifact PATH` instead of re-running the
               analysis (same identity check as explain --from).
               Stdin (--diff -) cannot verify a recorded diff identity;
               create and reuse the artifact with a named --diff PATH.
               --max-related-tests still applies, including beyond the
               check --json render cap.
  --mode MODE  How much of the workspace is indexed: instant (changed
               files only, cheapest), draft (packages the diff touches; the
               default), fast (same as draft for now), deep and ready (whole
               workspace, slowest). See docs/CONFIGURATION.md "Analysis
               modes". With --from, this feeds the identity recomputation
               (see `ripr explain --help`).
  --no-unchanged-tests
               Limit the index to changed Rust files. With --from, feeds
               the identity recomputation (see `ripr explain --help`).
  --perl-facts PATH
               Use this Perl facts file for replay.
  --suppression-policy PATH
               Apply the explicit suppression policy for replay.
  --json       Output is already JSON; passing it also makes usage errors
               and selector misses print a `cli_refusal` JSON document.
  --quiet      Suppress analysis progress and heartbeats on stderr, like
               `ripr check --quiet`. Does not change stdout, exit codes, or
               error reporting.

Exit status:
  0  the JSON packet was printed
  2  usage error (no selector, conflicting flags), a selector that matches
     no finding or several, or a failed analysis. Once the arguments are
     accepted, a failure also prints a JSON refusal document on stdout.
     Usage errors and selector misses keep stdout empty unless `--json` is
     passed, which prints the `cli_refusal` document instead.

Filesystem effects:
  Fresh analysis may create or refresh disposable cache files under
  target/ripr/cache/ (or RIPR_CACHE_DIR when set).

Performance:
  Use --from to skip re-analysis when you already ran
  `ripr check --write-artifact PATH` (see `ripr explain --help`).

Examples:
  ripr context --at <finding-id>
```

### continue

`ripr help continue`

```text
After the test edit, check whether it closed the gap.

Run this after `ripr repair` has named a gap (changed behavior no current test
appears to check) and you have edited the focused test it pointed at. ripr
re-reads your tests, compares the evidence with what it recorded when the
repair started, and writes a receipt: a JSON record of the before and after
result. ripr does not run your tests and never edits your source or test files.

Usage: ripr continue [--attempt ID] [--root PATH] [--json] [--quiet]

Options:
  --attempt ID     Continue this repair attempt. Without it, continue runs
                   only when exactly one current attempt exists under the
                   root; with several it lists them with a retry command
                   and picks none.
  --root PATH      Workspace root. Defaults to the current directory, then
                   walks up to the enclosing workspace or package, or the git
                   top level; `--root .` pins this directory.
  --json           Print the result as JSON, or the attempt's status JSON
                   when it is already complete. A refusal or failure inside
                   the check also prints its JSON document on stdout
                   (`repair_after_refusal`, `repair_after_failure`, or the
                   verify document) beside the stderr prose and the same
                   exit code. Refusals that stop before the check (no
                   current attempt, several attempts, an ended attempt, a
                   blocked baseline, an unanchored root) and operational
                   errors before the verify step keep stdout empty. An
                   unknown flag or stray argument prints the `cli_refusal`
                   JSON document on stdout beside its exit 2 stderr prose.
  --quiet          Drop progress lines and `wrote <path>` lines from stderr.
                   Refusals and the result stay. `RIPR_QUIET` does the same.

What it checks, in order:
  1. Nothing moved underneath: HEAD and the analysis inputs still match the
     start of the attempt.
  2. Only the test file (or inline test module) the repair allowed changed.
  3. Whether the static evidence now shows a test that would notice the
     changed behavior being wrong. The receipt records the answer.
A moved HEAD, changed analysis input, or refused verification stops with a
named refusal and the command to restart or recover.

An attempt that is already confirmed complete prints its status and exits 0
without running again. One that ended without a receipt (stale, failed, or
incomparable), or finished without a receipt that confirms it (unissued,
unavailable, or compatibility-only), prints its state and exits 3; no
completion is claimed.

Exit status:
  0  the check ran and wrote its result, or the attempt was already complete
  2  usage or operational error, or the edit check rejected the attempt:
     files outside the allowed test changed, HEAD moved, or the files could
     not be compared (that attempt is over; start again with `ripr repair`)
  3  a named refusal, such as no edit yet (make it and rerun); for a coded
     refusal, stderr ends with `ripr: refusal code=<code> disposition=<disposition>`

The advanced spelling `ripr agent repair --attempt ID --phase after` runs the
same step.

Examples:
  ripr continue [--attempt ID] --root .
```

### coverage-grip

Shared help for `ripr coverage-grip`, `ripr coverage-grip frontier`.

```text
Report whether line coverage and behavior evidence moved together.

Usage: ripr coverage-grip frontier (--ledger PATH|--baseline-delta PATH|--zero-status PATH) [--coverage PATH] [--out PATH] [--out-md PATH]

Frontier options:
  --coverage PATH          Optional coverage summary JSON.
  --ledger PATH            Optional PR evidence ledger JSON from `ripr pr-ledger record`.
  --baseline-delta PATH    Optional baseline-debt-delta JSON from `ripr baseline diff`.
  --zero-status PATH       Optional RIPR Zero status JSON from `ripr zero status`.
  --out PATH               JSON output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/coverage-grip-frontier.json.
  --out-md PATH            Markdown output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/coverage-grip-frontier.md.

The coverage/grip frontier report is read-only advisory evidence. It keeps
line execution coverage and RIPR behavioral grip movement as separate axes. It
does not treat coverage as adequacy, run mutation testing, change gate policy,
or make CI blocking by default.

Examples:
  ripr coverage-grip frontier --ledger target/ripr/reports/pr-evidence-ledger.json
```

### diff

`ripr help diff`

```text
Analyze the changed surface first and report full-repo context as an explicit bounded state.

Usage: ripr diff [--root PATH] [--base REV] [--head REV] [--mode MODE] [--format FORMAT] [--json]

Options:
  --root PATH              Workspace root. Defaults to the current directory, then
                           walks up to the enclosing workspace or package, or the git
                           top level; `--root .` pins this directory.
  --base REV               Base revision for git diff. When omitted, resolved
                           like check: the local origin/HEAD ref, then
                           origin/main, origin/master, main, and master.
  --head REV               Head revision for git diff. Defaults to HEAD.
  --mode MODE              instant, draft, fast, deep, or ready. Defaults to draft.
  --format FORMAT          human, text, md, markdown, or json. Defaults to human.
  --json                   Shortcut for --format json.
  --no-unchanged-tests     Limit the index to changed Rust files.

The diff report emits changed files, changed seams, static evidence for those
seams, the diff runtime status, an explicit full-repo-limited context
status, and a receipt path hint. It does not run mutation testing, edit files,
or turn the full-repo limitation into a success state.

Exit status:
  Complete and partial_with_limitations reports exit 0, regardless of findings.
  `unsupported_input` reports exit 2 after the original report is written;
  limitations and recovery routes remain available in that report. Usage and
  operational errors also exit 2. An empty diff is complete no_scope (exit 0).
  Diagnostic prose stays on stderr; JSON stdout contains one report.

Examples:
  ripr diff --root . --base REV --head HEAD --json
```

### doctor

`ripr help doctor`

```text
Diagnose the local ripr setup (workspace, config, toolchains, paths).

Usage: ripr doctor [--root PATH] [--json] [--timings] [--profile analysis|source-build]

Options:
  --root PATH   Diagnose the selected workspace (defaults to `.`).
  --json        Emit the core checks as stable JSON and use the same exit status.
  --timings     With --json, include the volatile timing fields (elapsed_ms,
                segments). Default --json output is byte-stable across runs
                that changed nothing: timing fields are omitted. The human
                screen always prints its run-time summary; --timings only
                affects --json.
  --profile NAME  Select the doctor profile: analysis (default; checks the
                  installed binary) or source-build (prerequisites for
                  building RIPR from source).

Environment variables:
  RIPR_CACHE_DIR  Relocate the cache base directory (all cache reads and
                  writes use this path instead of the default
                  {workspace_root}/target/ripr/cache). Useful for read-only
                  or immutable source checkouts and for redirecting the
                  cache to a faster or larger volume. Unset or empty keeps
                  the default. Example:
                  RIPR_CACHE_DIR=/var/cache/ripr ripr check

Default human output fits one 80x24 screen: failures first, each with a Fix
line, then compact passing groups. `-v`/`--verbose` prints binary identity,
config defaults, test surfaces, Perl preview, known limitations, and start-here
detail. `--json` remains the full JSON report minus the volatile timing
fields; pass `--timings` with `--json` to include them.

The JSON report is machine-readable advisory setup evidence. A `fail` status
means at least one core check failed; it is not a release or gate decision.
A completed run with failed checks exits 3; exit 2 means the run could not
complete (for example a usage error, where no check ran).

Marks: `!` is a blocking failure that fails the run (exit 3); `~` is an
advisory (for example artifacts under target/ripr not covered by git ignore
rules, tracked artifacts, an unwritable cache, unanalyzed languages) and never
changes the exit status.

Checks:
  - root directory exists
  - Cargo.toml is present at the selected root, an ancestor Cargo project
    bounded by git, or a nested Cargo.toml in this tree (when Rust is in
    scope)
  - ripr.toml load status and effective defaults are visible
  - git is available; cargo and rustc availability is disclosed when Rust is
    in scope. Missing tools or an older workspace rustc are advisory for
    installed-binary static analysis, but fail the source-build profile.
    Missing cargo or rustc on --profile source-build names an install route
    on the `!` line (https://rustup.rs or the OS package manager). An older
    rustc still names `rustup update stable`. Project verification uses the
    project's selected toolchain and its actual execution result; doctor does
    not run verification.

Rust is in scope when it is enabled and Cargo.toml is found at the selected
root, an ancestor Cargo project bounded by git, or nested in this tree; when
.rs files are detected at the selected root; or when no other language is
detected or enabled. Otherwise (for example a Python-only or TypeScript-only
root with no nested or ancestor Cargo.toml) the analysis profile skips the
Cargo.toml, cargo, and rustc checks with the reason and does not fail doctor.
`--profile source-build` still runs cargo and rustc checks.

First-run diagnosis:
  - Detected languages: shallow file-marker scan; each language shows its
    canonical tier (stable or preview) and [adapter not compiled] when the
    feature is absent. Only languages with concrete markers are listed —
    no overclaiming. Printed for every profile.
  - Detected test surfaces: per detected language, the first recognizable
    framework marker (cargo test, pytest, jest, vitest, bun). Prints
    "test framework not detected" rather than guessing. Printed with
    `-v`/`--verbose`.
  - Known limitations: static notes on preview coverage, cross-language
    oracle visibility (unknown is never assumed safe), large-repo scan bounds, and advisory
    nature of preview-language evidence. Printed with `-v`/`--verbose`.
  - Recommended first command (analysis profile; not printed for --profile
    source-build): ripr check (no base: the loader resolves this
    repository's own default branch). When git is not on PATH, the `!` git line
    names install git or `--diff PATH` / `--diff -`, and the recommended
    command is `ripr check --diff PATH`. Outside a Git work tree it names the
    repository-free scan, and a missing root is named in the recovery command
    through its lossless spelling.

Start-here next step (analysis profile; not printed for --profile source-build):
  - open `target/ripr/reports/start-here.md` first when it exists
  - when it does not, run `ripr check` first: `ripr first-pr` and
    `ripr start-here` compose that packet from analysis evidence and run no
    analysis of their own, so on a fresh workspace they report
    `missing_artifacts`
  - to compose or refresh the packet, run
    `ripr first-pr --root . --base <ref> --head HEAD`
    or `ripr start-here --root . --base <ref> --head HEAD`
    or this repo's `cargo xtask first-pr` wrapper
  - safe next action means repair one named gap, regenerate missing or malformed
    evidence, refresh stale evidence, fix wrong-root setup, or stop on no-action
  - treat missing artifact, stale evidence, wrong root, malformed artifact,
    no actionable gap, and preview-limited evidence as explicit stop or
    regeneration states, not hidden success
  - verify command, receipt command, and receipt path are the static proof rail;
    receipts stay advisory and do not prove runtime adequacy or gate approval

Examples:
  ripr doctor
```

### evidence-health

`ripr help evidence-health`

```text
Summarize how strong the current static evidence looks across the workspace.

Usage: ripr evidence-health [--root PATH] [--out PATH] [--out-md PATH] [--mutation-calibration PATH] [--quiet]

Options:
  --root PATH                    Workspace root to summarize. Defaults to current directory.
  --out PATH                     JSON output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/evidence-health.json.
  --out-md PATH                  Markdown output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/evidence-health.md.
  --mutation-calibration PATH    Optional imported mutation-calibration JSON for calibration availability counts.
  --quiet                        Silence the stderr progress lines (also RIPR_QUIET).

The evidence-health report is an advisory Lane 1 analyzer-health view. It
summarizes seam grip classes, missing discriminators, observed values, related
test confidence, oracle strength, unknown static stages, and optional imported
calibration availability. It does not change analyzer behavior, run mutation
testing, edit source files, configure CI policy, or make gate decisions.

Examples:
  ripr evidence-health --root PATH
```

### explain

`ripr help explain`

```text
Print why ripr flagged a specific change.

Usage: ripr explain [--root PATH] [--base REV] [--worktree|--committed|--diff PATH] [--from PATH] [--path GLOB] [--exclude GLOB] [--mode MODE] [--no-unchanged-tests] [--perl-facts PATH] [--suppression-policy PATH] [--format human|agent] [--quiet] <finding-id|file:line>

Options:
  --root PATH  Workspace root. Defaults to the current directory, then
               walks up to the enclosing workspace or package, or the git
               top level; `--root .` pins this directory. A member-relative
               `file:line` selector binds to the directory you ran from and
               is refused when a workspace-root file with the same path
               suffix exists, even without a root finding there (use
               `--root .` or a finding ID; with
               --from or --diff, a selector naming no file is anchored to that
               directory).
  --format F   human (default; text is an alias) or agent. agent prints the selected finding as
               compact `check --format agent` lines (one record, its related
               test, and an explicit done=/open=/stop= terminal line plus
               next=<ripr context command>), static advisory only. For the
               JSON packet use `ripr context --at <finding-id>`.
  --quiet      Suppress analysis progress and heartbeats on stderr, like
               `ripr check --quiet`. Does not change stdout, exit codes, or
               error reporting.
  --base REV   Compare against this revision, as in `ripr check --base`.
               Not combinable with --diff unless --from is also given.
  --diff PATH  Read a diff file instead of running git diff (`-` = stdin).
  --committed  Analyze committed history only (base...HEAD), even when the
               working tree is dirty. Not combinable with --worktree, --diff
               or --from. Without a supplied scope, dirty repositories use
               the same worktree default as `ripr check`.
  --worktree   Analyze staged and unstaged tracked edits, like
               `ripr check --worktree`, so a finding listed from uncommitted
               edits can be selected. Not combinable with --diff or --from.
  --path GLOB  Analyze only changed files matching GLOB (repeatable). Same
               patterns and intake filter as `ripr check --path`. A scoped
               `ripr check` prints this flag on its explain drill-in so the
               pasted command does not re-analyze the full oversized diff.
  --exclude GLOB
               Skip changed files matching GLOB (repeatable; wins over
               --path). Same patterns as `ripr check --exclude`.
  --from PATH  Load findings from a check artifact written by
               `ripr check --write-artifact PATH` instead of re-running the
               analysis. The artifact's recorded diff source is re-resolved
               and its identity is re-verified; any mismatch (diff, root,
               mode, languages, analysis options, config identity, or
               analyzer version) stops with an error naming the
               mismatched fields. --diff/--base passed alongside --from are
               assertions verified against the recording, not overrides.
               Stdin (--diff -) cannot verify a recorded diff identity;
               create and reuse the artifact with a named --diff PATH.
  --mode MODE  instant, draft, fast, deep, or ready. Defaults to draft.
               With --from, this feeds the identity recomputation: an
               artifact written with a non-default --mode is consumable only
               when the same mode resolves here (flag or ripr.toml).
  --no-unchanged-tests
               Limit the index to changed Rust files. With --from, an
               artifact written with this flag is consumable only when the
               same setting resolves here (flag or ripr.toml).
  --perl-facts PATH
               Use this Perl facts file for replay.
  --suppression-policy PATH
               Apply the explicit suppression policy for replay.

Filesystem effects:
  Fresh analysis may create or refresh disposable cache files under
  target/ripr/cache/ (or RIPR_CACHE_DIR when set).

Performance:
  Use --from to skip re-analysis when you already ran
  `ripr check --write-artifact PATH`. This avoids re-parsing the diff and
  re-classifying every changed behavior — useful for large diffs and scripted workflows
  that run check, explain, and context in sequence.

Examples:
  ripr explain <finding-id|file:line> --base REV
```

### feedback

`ripr help feedback`

```text
Record local usefulness feedback against an immutable analysis result.

Usage:
  ripr feedback record --snapshot ID --reason CODE [--item ID] [--root PATH] [--json]
  ripr feedback export [--root PATH] [--route-quality PATH] [--out PATH] [--json]

`ripr feedback record` writes one versioned receipt under
`target/ripr/feedback/`. Recording is explicit: analyze, hover, and packet
paths never record feedback implicitly. Export joins stored receipts onto
existing route-quality rows without creating a second attempt ledger.

Writes:
  target/ripr/feedback/<idempotency-key>.json
  optional --out join document (export only)

Privacy:
  Stores references and reason codes, not source bodies, diffs, logs,
  environment values, or credentials. Notes are bounded and checked against
  known secret patterns (best-effort, not a guarantee). No network
  submission. Default storage is a local ignored artifact.

Exact output:
  JSON receipts use schema_version 0.1, kind usefulness_feedback_receipt.
  Export uses kind usefulness_feedback_join. Status is created or
  already_recorded. Conflict on the same idempotency key with a different
  payload exits non-zero.

Non-effects:
  Recording or aggregating feedback changes none of diagnostic visibility,
  analyzer classification, baseline/suppression/waiver policy, gap movement
  or closure, support tier, or CI gates. Agent feedback stays agent feedback
  until a human review actor is recorded. Silence is not a vote.

Run `ripr feedback record --help` or `ripr feedback export --help` for flags.

Examples:
  ripr feedback record --snapshot ID --reason CODE
  ripr feedback export --root .
```

### feedback-export

`ripr help feedback export`

```text
Join local usefulness-feedback receipts onto existing route-quality rows.

Usage: ripr feedback export [--root PATH] [--route-quality PATH] [--out PATH] [--json]

Options:
  --root PATH             Repository root. Default `.`. Reads
                          target/ripr/feedback/*.json.
  --route-quality PATH    Existing route-quality.json. Default
                          target/ripr/reports/route-quality.json. Missing input
                          still reports unmatched receipts; it does not invent
                          objective movement.
  --out PATH              Write the join JSON. Export is explicit and
                          previewable: omitting --out prints the document.
  --json                  Print JSON even when --out is set.

The join keeps objective route-quality counts separate from subjective
usefulness. Unreviewed, stale, unmatched, and missing-feedback states are
counts, not success percentages. Agent feedback is never relabelled
human-approved. No network, process, or policy mutation.

Examples:
  ripr feedback export --root .
```

### feedback-record

`ripr help feedback record`

```text
Record one local usefulness-feedback receipt bound to an immutable result.

Usage: ripr feedback record --snapshot ID --reason CODE [--item ID]
                            [--route-digest DIGEST] [--attempt ID] [--receipt ID]
                            [--actor human|agent|unknown]
                            [--review unreviewed|reviewed_accepted|reviewed_rejected]
                            [--review-actor human|agent|unknown]
                            [--judgment useful|incorrect|unclear|expensive|intentional_no_action]
                            [--note TEXT] [--idempotency-key KEY]
                            [--root PATH] [--json]

Options:
  --snapshot ID         Immutable analysis snapshot or result identity. Required.
  --item ID             Optional canonical item / gap id. Omit for useful
                        limitations and intentional no-action without a gap.
  --route-digest DIGEST Optional repair-route digest or kind used by join.
  --attempt ID          Optional RepairAttempt id. Historical after a later attempt.
  --receipt ID          Optional verify/receipt identity.
  --actor KIND          Who recorded this: human, agent, or unknown. Default unknown.
  --review STATUS       unreviewed (default), reviewed_accepted, or reviewed_rejected.
  --review-actor KIND   Required when --review is not unreviewed.
  --reason CODE         Closed taxonomy (useful_actionable, useful_limitation,
                        wrong_target, wrong_discriminator, false_actionable,
                        unclear_explanation, too_slow, intentional_defensive_code,
                        other, ...). `other` requires --note and --judgment.
  --judgment CLASS      Required for --reason other. Must match the reason class
                        otherwise.
  --note TEXT           Optional bounded note (1024 bytes). Fail-closed on known
                        secret patterns. Best-effort, not a secret detector.
  --idempotency-key KEY Repeat of the same key and payload reuses one record.
                        A different payload with the same key is a conflict.
  --root PATH           Repository root. Default `.`. Writes
                        target/ripr/feedback/<key>.json.
  --json                Print the receipt JSON, including policy_effects unchanged.
  --file PATH           Rejected. Identity is --snapshot plus optional --item,
                        not a current file/line.
  --line N              Rejected. Identity is --snapshot plus optional --item,
                        not a current file/line.

Non-effects: does not suppress findings, change classification, rewrite
baselines, waive gates, close gaps, or contact a network. File/line is not
accepted as identity.

Examples:
  ripr feedback record --snapshot ID --reason CODE
```

### first-action

`ripr help first-action`

```text
Recommend the next focused test to add from existing review artifacts.

Usage: ripr first-action [--root PATH] [--pr-guidance PATH] [--assistant-proof PATH] [--gap-ledger PATH] [--ledger PATH] [--baseline-delta PATH] [--receipt PATH] [--gate-decision PATH] [--coverage-frontier PATH] [--editor-context PATH] [--out PATH] [--out-md PATH]

At least one artifact input is required. Each one below is individually
optional, but `ripr first-action` with none exits 2 rather than guessing where
artifacts live, so the paths printed in `ripr help --all` are examples of what
to pass, not defaults that are read for you.

Options:
  --root PATH                Workspace root label. Defaults to current directory.
  --pr-guidance PATH         Optional PR guidance JSON from `ripr review-comments`.
  --assistant-proof PATH     Optional proof JSON from `ripr assistant-loop proof`.
  --gap-ledger PATH          Optional gap decision ledger JSON from `ripr reports gap-ledger`.
  --ledger PATH              Optional PR evidence ledger JSON from `ripr pr-ledger record`.
  --baseline-delta PATH      Optional baseline-debt-delta JSON from `ripr baseline diff`.
  --receipt PATH             Optional agent receipt JSON from `ripr agent receipt`.
  --gate-decision PATH       Optional gate-decision JSON from `ripr gate evaluate`.
  --coverage-frontier PATH   Optional coverage/grip frontier JSON.
  --editor-context PATH      Optional editor evidence context packet JSON.
  --out PATH                 JSON output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/first-useful-action.json.
  --out-md PATH              Markdown output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/first-useful-action.md.

The first-action report is a read-only advisory router over explicit existing
RIPR artifacts. It writes one next useful test action or one fallback reason
for developers, reviewers, or coding agents. It does not rerun analysis, post
comments, edit source, generate tests, call a provider, run mutation testing,
invent policy, or make CI blocking by default.

Start-here vocabulary:
  - safe next action means add one focused proof, refresh missing/stale/wrong-root/malformed evidence, or stop on no-action.
  - verify command, receipt command, and receipt path are static movement evidence, not runtime adequacy.
  - preview-limited evidence stays advisory and must show static limits before repair language.

Examples:
  ripr first-action --pr-guidance target/ripr/review/comments.json
```

### first-pr

Shared help for `ripr first-pr`, `ripr start-here`.

```text
Summarize what to fix in one PR from existing ripr reports.

Answers "what should I do first on this PR?" first-pr reads reports that
earlier ripr commands wrote (check output, the gap list, review comments,
receipts) and writes one start-here page (the start-here packet:
start-here.md and start-here.json), naming a single next step. A gap is
changed behavior that no current test appears to check. By default first-pr runs no analysis: for a missing report
it prints the command that creates it. Pass --run-chain to run those commands.

Usage: ripr first-pr|start-here [--root <path>] [--base <rev>] [--head <rev>] [--check-output <path>] [--gap-ledger <path>] [--first-action <path>] [--review-comments <path>] [--agent-packet <path>] [--gate-decision <path>] [--receipts-dir <path>] [--out-dir <path>] [--check] [--run-chain]

Options:
  --root <path>              Workspace root. Defaults to .
  --base <rev>               PR base revision. When omitted, resolved like
                             `ripr check`: origin/HEAD, then origin/main,
                             origin/master, main, and master.
  --head <rev>               PR head revision. Defaults to HEAD.
  --check-output <path>      Existing `ripr check --json` output to build the gap list from.
                             Without --run-chain, first-pr never runs analysis itself.
  --gap-ledger <path>        Gap list (gap-decision ledger) JSON. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/gap-decision-ledger.json.
  --first-action <path>      First-useful-action JSON. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/first-useful-action.json.
  --review-comments <path>   Review-comments JSON. Defaults to target/ripr/review/comments.json.
  --agent-packet <path>      Agent handoff JSON. Defaults to target/ripr/workflow/agent-packet.json.
  --gate-decision <path>     Gate-decision JSON. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/gate-decision.json.
  --receipts-dir <path>      Directory of repair receipts (before/after records). Defaults to target/ripr/receipts.
  --out-dir <path>           Output directory. Defaults to target/ripr/reports.
  --check                    Verify the existing start-here page is up to date; write nothing.
  --run-chain                Run the commands for missing reports first, each only when its
                             report is missing and each exactly the command first-pr prints,
                             with the resolved --base and --head: the repo-exposure report (a
                             `ripr check` run on a Python or TypeScript root without a Cargo
                             manifest), the gap list, then the review cards. This runs analysis
                             (cost scales with the repository), writes the missing reports (by
                             default under target/ripr/) and uses no network. The first failing
                             step stops with exit 2 and no start-here page is written from
                             partial reports. Cannot be combined with --check or --check-output.

Exit status:
  0  the start-here page was written, or --check found a current, unblocked page
  2  usage error, unresolvable input, or --check found a missing, stale or malformed page,
     or a current page that records a blocked state (wrong root, missing or malformed reports)
  Write mode exits 0 after composing a page, including a recovery page; read its
  State line (or the JSON `selected.output_state`), or run --check, to gate on
  the page state.

Start-here language:
  - start here: open target/ripr/reports/start-here.md first when it exists
  - safe next action: fix one named gap, regenerate a missing report, or stop because nothing needs doing
  - missing artifact / stale evidence / wrong root / malformed artifact: a report is absent, out of date,
    from another directory or unreadable; first-pr stops before suggesting any fix
  - no actionable gap: nothing to fix was found; advisory, not a promise that the tests catch every bug
  - preview-limited evidence: from a syntax-only preview analysis; advisory, with its limits stated before any fix
  - receipt lifecycle: receipt_missing, receipt_found, receipt_stale, receipt_gap_mismatch, receipt_movement_improved, receipt_movement_unchanged, receipt_not_applicable
  - verify command / receipt command / receipt path: the commands that recheck a fix and record its
    before/after result, and where that record is written

Examples:
  ripr first-pr --root . --base BASE --head HEAD
```

### gate

Shared help for `ripr gate`, `ripr gate check`, `ripr gate evaluate`.

```text
Evaluate the optional pass/fail gate against existing PR guidance (advisory unless explicitly enabled).

Usage: ripr gate evaluate [--pr-guidance PATH | --gap-ledger PATH] [--mode MODE] [--out PATH] [--out-md PATH] [further inputs: see Options below]
       ripr gate check --base REV [--head REV] [--mode MODE] [--label LABEL]... [--labels-json PATH] [check options: see below]

`gate check` is the one-command CI gate: it runs `ripr review-comments` for
--base..--head, then `gate evaluate` over the guidance it wrote, and exits like
`gate evaluate`: 0 pass/advisory/acknowledged, 3 blocked, 2 config_error. It
defaults to --mode acknowledgeable, so an eligible new gap blocks unless the PR
carries the waiver label. If review-comments cannot complete, the previous
guidance document is not reused: the decision is config_error (exit 2).

Check options:
  --base REV                          Required. Base revision of the change, for example origin/main.
  --head REV                          Head revision. Defaults to HEAD.
  --timeout-ms N                      Passed to review-comments.
  --guidance-out PATH                 Guidance JSON path. Defaults to target/ripr/review/comments.json.
                                      Any existing file there (and its .md) is removed before the
                                      run, and again if review-comments fails.
  --mode MODE                         Same modes as gate evaluate, but defaults to acknowledgeable.
  --root, --label, --labels-json, --acknowledgement-label, --exception-policy,
  --acknowledgements, --baseline, --out, --out-md
                                      As for gate evaluate.

gate check produces its own guidance, so it does not accept --pr-guidance,
--gap-ledger or the other evaluate-only inputs (--repo-exposure, --sarif-policy,
--agent-verify, --agent-receipt, --recommendation-calibration, --mutation-calibration);
run review-comments and gate evaluate yourself to supply them.

Evaluate options:
  --root PATH                         Workspace root. Must be an existing directory. Defaults to current directory.
  --repo-exposure PATH                Optional repo-exposure JSON input.
  --pr-guidance PATH                  Optional PR guidance JSON from `ripr review-comments`.
  --gap-ledger PATH                   Optional gap decision ledger JSON; when supplied, gate candidates come from repairable GapRecord projection targets.
  --sarif-policy PATH                 Optional SARIF policy JSON input.
  --labels-json PATH                  Optional JSON array or object with labels.
  --label LABEL                       Repeatable current PR label input.
  --agent-verify PATH                 Optional agent verify JSON input.
  --agent-receipt PATH                Optional agent receipt JSON input.
  --recommendation-calibration PATH   Optional recommendation calibration JSON input.
  --mutation-calibration PATH         Optional imported mutation calibration JSON input.
  --baseline PATH                     Explicit baseline for baseline-check or calibrated-gate.
  --exception-policy PATH             Optional quality-gate-exceptions TOML ledger. Enforces
                                      per-exception expiry (expired entries block), review-after
                                      deadlines (block or warn per the ledger's due_review),
                                      required_active entries (missing ones block), and
                                      status = "final" ledgers (any active exception blocks).
                                      Active exceptions and violations are reported in the
                                      gate-decision JSON and Markdown. A missing or malformed
                                      ledger is a config_error (fail-closed).
  --acknowledgements PATH             Optional structured acknowledgement ledger (TOML,
                                      schema_version = 1). Scoped rows bind to canonical_gap_id;
                                      legacy labels retain global compatibility disclosure.
  --mode MODE                         visible-only, acknowledgeable, baseline-check, or calibrated-gate. Defaults to visible-only.
  --acknowledgement-label LABEL       Repeatable acknowledgement label. Defaults to ripr-waive.
  --out PATH                          JSON output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/gate-decision.json.
  --out-md PATH                       Markdown output path. Defaults to --out with .md extension.

The gate evaluator is read-only policy over existing RIPR evidence. It writes
JSON and Markdown before returning exit 3 for a completed `blocked` decision
or exit 2 for a completed `config_error` (evaluation could not complete). A
`--root` that does not exist or is not a directory fails closed with exit 2
and a message naming the root; evaluation does not start and no decision
report is written. It does not post comments, edit source,
generate tests, run mutation testing, upload SARIF, mutate GitHub state, or
change generated workflow defaults.

Output discipline: JSON and Markdown are written to `--out` and `--out-md`
(with the documented defaults); stdout contains human `Wrote ...` status lines,
not the JSON report. Capture the report files for machine consumers. When
`--mode` is omitted and stderr is non-interactive, ripr prints a warning that
the visible-only default records evidence without blocking, after a completed
evaluation. Missing-input usage errors and `config_error` reports stay quiet.
An explicit `--mode visible-only` is quiet; blocking modes remain opt-in.

Examples:
  ripr gate
  ripr gate evaluate --pr-guidance PATH
  ripr gate check --base origin/main
```

### help

`ripr help help`

```text
ripr — find changed code where nearby tests may not actually catch the
       changed behavior (Rust; Python and TypeScript in preview).

Usage:
  ripr <command> [options]

Try this first:
  ripr check                      Analyze the current diff, name the top gap.

Uses tracked edits, or committed history when clean. On a clean base branch,
edit a tracked source file first; new files need git add -N PATH.

The loop is: ripr names one gap -> you add one focused test -> ripr records
whether the gap closed. Commit your source change first, so `ripr repair` can
tell your new test apart from it. `ripr.toml` is optional; the zero-config run
is the intended first interface.

What are you trying to do?
  Diagnose setup        ripr doctor
  Inspect one change    ripr check [--base REV | --diff PATH]
                                   [--format human-full | json]
  Guided repo adoption  ripr pilot --root .
  Understand a finding  ripr explain <finding-id>
                        ripr context --at <finding-id>
  Repair a Rust gap     ripr repair [<item>]
                        # edit one focused test
                        ripr continue
  Repair a diff gap     follow the start from ripr check, when offered
  Compose PR evidence   ripr first-pr --root . --base BASE --head HEAD
  Work in an editor     ripr lsp --stdio (started by your editor)
  Adopt advisory CI     ripr init --ci github
  Wire up your agent    ripr init --agents all   (docs/AGENT_QUICKSTART.md)

More:
  ripr help <command>    Options for one command.
  ripr help --all        Every command, grouped by area.
  ripr help --json       Versioned machine-readable command catalog.

Exit codes: 0 completed, 2 could not complete (usage, configuration, or
operational error), 3 ripr declined: a blocking result, or a request it will
not run (the output says why), 130 interrupted standalone check. Full
contract: docs/EXIT_CODES.md.
Global flags: -v, --verbose   Extra pipeline diagnostics on stderr: analyzed
languages, mode, and counts (any position, except on `ripr help --json`).

ripr reads your changed code, imagines small bugs in it, and checks whether
your tests would likely catch them. It does not run mutants or your tests and
reports no runtime outcomes; a real mutation runner confirms later.
```

`ripr help impacted-evidence`

```text
Route mutation mode from PR evidence and PR labels.

Usage: ripr impacted-evidence [--pr-evidence <path>] [--label <label>] [--labels <csv>] [--check]

Options:
  --pr-evidence <path>  Path to repo-exposure.json (default: target/ripr/pr/repo-exposure.json)
  --label <label>       Add a single PR label (repeatable)
  --labels <csv>        Add comma/newline/semicolon-separated PR labels
  --check               Verify outputs are up to date

Outputs:

  target/xtask/impacted-evidence/latest.md
```

### init

`ripr help init`

```text
Write an optional repo policy file (ripr.toml) and, with --ci, a non-blocking advisory CI preset.

Usage: ripr init [--root PATH] [--ci github|gitlab] [--mcp] [--agents claude|codex|cursor|all] [--dry-run] [--force]

`ripr init` is optional. It writes the built-in defaults to a repo-local
ripr.toml so teams can commit, review, and tune policy. Missing ripr.toml is
the normal first-run state and uses the same defaults. Running `ripr init` does
not unlock basic CLI, editor, or pilot usefulness.

Options:
  --root PATH      Workspace root where ripr.toml should be written. Defaults to current directory.
  --ci PROVIDER    Also write an advisory CI preset: github writes .github/workflows/ripr.yml;
                   gitlab writes .gitlab-ci.yml with a merge-request check and review-comments flow.
  --mcp            Also add the ripr MCP server to .mcp.json (Claude Code project config).
                   Other servers in an existing file are kept; an existing
                   `ripr` entry is kept unless --force; a symlink or a file
                   that is not a JSON object is refused. The file is rewritten
                   with sorted keys. Like --ci, --mcp keeps an existing
                   ripr.toml and --force does not reset it. Codex config is
                   user-global and is never written: init prints the
                   `codex mcp add` command.
  --agents TARGET  Also add a short ripr loop (find a gap, write a test, verify,
                   explicit done and stop rules) for your coding agent: claude
                   -> CLAUDE.md, codex -> AGENTS.md, cursor ->
                   .cursor/rules/ripr.mdc, all -> all three. Repeatable. The
                   text goes in a marked section appended to your file; your
                   other content is never touched, a rerun changes nothing,
                   and an edited section is kept unless --force refreshes it.
                   A symlink, an unreadable file or an unterminated marker is
                   refused. With cursor, --mcp also writes .cursor/mcp.json.
                   Guide: docs/AGENT_QUICKSTART.md.
  --dry-run       Show the plan and the file bodies without writing anything.
                   Resolves the same preconditions as the real run, so it
                   fails the same way (existing file without --force, root
                   that is not a directory) instead of reporting success.
  --force          Replace what init would otherwise refuse or keep. Plain `ripr init --force`
                   resets an existing ripr.toml. With --ci, --mcp or --agents, ripr.toml is
                   always kept; --force then only replaces the generated workflow,
                   the `ripr` entry in .mcp.json, or the marked agent section.

Generated config:
  - uses draft analysis mode and includes unchanged tests
  - shows actionable weak or missing seams with default severities
  - hides seams whose configured severity is off
  - records the built-in saved-workspace LSP seam diagnostic default
  - remains advisory and does not configure CI blocking or mutation execution

Generated GitHub workflow (--ci github):
  - installs ripr and runs `ripr reports ci-packet` for the PR evidence packet
  - uploads report artifacts and writes a reviewer-oriented advisory summary
  - optionally renders inline review comments (RIPR_COMMENT_MODE=inline)
  - renders and uploads diff/repo SARIF only while RIPR_UPLOAD_SARIF is true
  - uses continue-on-error for advisory RIPR work and upload steps
  - does not enable baseline failure policy by default

Generated GitLab pipeline (--ci gitlab):
  - runs on merge-request pipelines only with allow_failure: true
  - installs the pinned ripr release, runs `ripr check` and `ripr review-comments`
  - uploads target/ripr/** artifacts for review (no SARIF or MR comment publishing)

Examples:
  ripr init
```

### lsp

`ripr help lsp`

```text
Start the experimental ripr LSP server over stdio.

Usage: ripr lsp [--stdio] [--version]

Options:
  --stdio       Run the language server over stdio LSP framing. This is the default.
  --version     Print the language server version.

Server-executed commands (workspace/executeCommand), with their arguments:
  ripr.refresh                  no arguments; re-runs analysis with the full seam inventory
  ripr.collectContext           one object: {"finding_id": "probe:..."},
                                {"seam_id": "...", "evidence_identity": {...}}, or
                                {"gap_id": "...", "gap_ledger": "..."} (gap_ledger optional)
  ripr.collectEvidenceContext   one object: {"seam_id": "...", "evidence_identity": {...}}
  ripr.collectRepairPacket      no arguments for the top packet, or {"gap_id": "..."}
  ripr.collectWorkspaceStatus   no arguments
  ripr.collectTopLimitation     no arguments
  ripr.collectReceiptStatus     no arguments
  ripr.showRelatedTest          one object: {"uri": "file:///...", "line": N, "input_identity": "..."};
                                asks the client to open the related test via window/showDocument

  Copy ids and evidence_identity from a ripr diagnostic's data. A shape the
  server cannot read, or an id missing from the current snapshot, is a
  -32602 InvalidParams error that names the accepted shapes; it is never null.
  `ripr/listActionableItems` (custom request) lists the delivered and
  omitted diagnostics by canonical id, and under `hidden_gaps` the gaps the
  default actionable profile never publishes because they have no repair
  route, such as a new function no test calls. Each listed canonical id and
  hidden-gap finding_id is accepted by `ripr.collectContext` (seam ids
  together with the envelope's `seam_evidence_identity`). Set `[lsp]
  diagnostic_profile = "full"` in ripr.toml to publish those as diagnostics
  too.

Examples:
  ripr lsp --stdio
```

### mcp

`ripr help mcp`

```text
Expose RIPR's bounded, read-only workspace session over the Model Context Protocol.

Usage: ripr mcp [--stdio] [--root PATH]

Options:
  --stdio       Serve newline-delimited MCP JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout. This is
                the default and only transport in the supported slices.
  --root PATH   Use this exact repository root. Without it, RIPR starts at the
                current directory and walks ancestors to the nearest supported
                repository marker.
  --help, -h    Print this help.
  --version, -V Print the MCP server version.

The MCP surface is read-only. It exposes tools `ripr_workspace_status`,
`ripr_refresh`, `ripr_list_gaps`, `ripr_get_gap`, `ripr_get_top_limitation`,
`ripr_prepare_repair`,
`ripr_get_repair_attempt`, `ripr_get_receipt_status`,
`ripr_get_repair_card`, and `ripr_list_repair_attempts`, the resource
`ripr://workspace/status`, and the resource templates
`ripr://snapshot/{snapshot_id}`, `ripr://gap/{canonical_id}`,
`ripr://gap/{canonical_id}/limitation`, `ripr://repair-attempt/{attempt_id}`, `ripr://receipt/{receipt_id}`, and
`ripr://repair-card/{canonical_id}`.
`ripr_refresh` analyzes the default-branch diff through the shared check
authority; its optional `base` argument selects another revision. Like
`ripr check`, it reads saved staged and unstaged tracked edits when any exist
and committed input otherwise; `source: "committed"` or `source: "worktree"`
forces one; unsaved buffers and untracked files remain outside. Worktree cards
require established producer custody; otherwise withheld with the cause.
Readiness depends on per-item gates. Refresh after edits. Its warm cache lives
under the root's `target/ripr/`. Outside MCP, `ripr check --committed` reads
committed input and `ripr check --worktree --format json` saved tracked edits.
Gap tools read their captured snapshot and never re-run analysis.
`ripr_list_repair_attempts` discovers durable CLI attempts before or after
refresh, with bounded inventory-bound pages; it never creates the store.
`ripr_prepare_repair` evaluates producer
repair-readiness facts and may create one in-memory session repair
transaction; `ripr_get_repair_attempt` and `ripr_get_receipt_status` read
session transactions and the durable attempt store without executing
anything. `ripr_get_repair_card` projects the same bounded repair card as
`ripr agent card` and the standard-LSP handoff for one canonical item of the
completed session snapshot, assembled by the shared application authority;
it edits nothing, executes nothing, and never upgrades readiness or currentness.
The server does not edit source, execute verification or mutation
commands, launch processes, load project-local provider configuration, or
embed a model provider, and no evidence document is ever a repair
authorization. Protocol messages are the only stdout output. Operational
failures use stderr.

Examples:
  ripr mcp --stdio
```

### outcome

`ripr help outcome`

```text
Compare before/after static evidence after adding a focused test.

Usage: ripr outcome --before PATH --after PATH [--format md|markdown|text|json] [--out PATH]

Options:
  --before PATH    Static snapshot before the focused test: repo exposure or check JSON.
  --after PATH     Static snapshot after the focused test: repo exposure or check JSON.
  --format FORMAT  md, markdown, text, or json. Defaults to md.
  --out PATH       Write the rendered receipt to a file instead of stdout.

The outcome receipt is advisory. It compares static repo-exposure snapshots by
seam_id and check-output snapshots by canonical_gap_id, then reports moved,
unchanged, regressed, new, and removed gaps or seams. Rust `ripr check --json`
findings carry canonical_gap_id and are compared by it. Check output whose
findings carry no canonical_gap_id is refused rather than compared; repo
exposure carries no Python or TypeScript seams, so preview findings without a
canonical_gap_id have no comparable receipt. When head-identity verification
matters, capture both snapshots with `ripr check --format repo-exposure-json`,
because check JSON carries no repository head. The
review receipt summarizes what changed, what RIPR flagged before, which focused
proof signals moved, what remains weak or unknown, and what reviewers should
inspect or avoid inferring. It does not run analysis, edit source, generate
tests, run mutation testing, claim runtime correctness or coverage adequacy,
approve merges, or decide CI policy.

Limitation: the comparison matches seams/findings by id. Whether ripr can say
anything about provenance depends on the artifacts. A snapshot written through
the artifact-identity path, such as `ripr check --format repo-exposure-json`,
carries the repository head, and ripr reports on stderr whether the two
snapshots name the same head. A snapshot written without that identity,
including the `repo-exposure.json` that `ripr pilot` writes, carries no head;
ripr then says so and cannot verify the pair came from the same repository or
adjacent commits. Matching heads still do not mean matching working trees.

Examples:
  ripr outcome --before PATH --after PATH
```

### pilot

`ripr help pilot`

```text
Find the top test gap in this repo and write a packet you can act on.

Usage: ripr pilot [--root PATH] [--out PATH] [--mode MODE] [--max-seams N] [--timeout-ms MS] [--format FORMAT] [--quiet]

Options:
  --root PATH       Workspace root. Defaults to the current directory, then
                    walks up to the enclosing workspace or package, or the git
                    top level; `--root .` pins this directory.
  --out PATH        Output directory for the pilot packet. Defaults to
                    target/ripr/pilot under the resolved root (`--root .` pins
                    this directory).
  --mode MODE       instant, draft, fast, deep, or ready. Defaults to draft unless ripr.toml sets one.
  --max-seams N     Maximum ranked gaps in the pilot summary. Defaults to 5.
  --timeout-ms MS   Maximum analysis budget before writing a partial summary. Defaults to
                    30000; when the default passes, the same run continues for up to
                    240000 more (270000 ms total from start, plus up to about 5 s of
                    cancel grace before the partial summary is written). An explicit value
                    is a hard limit with no extension.
  --format FORMAT   human (default) or json. `--format json` writes the same
                    pilot-summary.json document to stdout and suppresses the
                    human terminal; packet files are still written.
  --quiet           Suppress analysis progress and heartbeats on stderr. Does not
                    change the pilot packet, exit codes, or error reporting.

Progress:
  Long-running pilot analysis writes producer stages to stderr as
  `ripr progress: <stage> [repo]` and, while a stage stays active, throttled
  `still active after <elapsed class>` heartbeats, exactly as `ripr check`
  reports them, including `processed_<n>_of_<total>` once the inventory has
  an honest seam denominator. Non-TTY / CI output is newline-delimited with
  no control sequences; stdout and the pilot packet stay byte-clean. When
  the default timeout passes, the same run continues under the same progress
  stream. `--quiet` turns this stream off.

Environment variables:
  RIPR_PILOT_SEAM_BUDGET        Maximum gaps written to pilot artifacts (repo-exposure.json,
                                 agent-seam-packets.json). Default: 2000. Set to 0 to disable
                                 the budget and write all gaps (may produce very large files).
                                 When the budget is applied, both artifacts include a
                                 limitations[] disclosure naming the env var and a repair route.
  RIPR_PILOT_REPO_EXPOSURE_BYTES Byte budget for the entries in repo-exposure.json. Default:
                                 8000000 (the entry count alone let it reach 13 MB). A cut sets
                                 run_status limited_repo_exposure_bytes, reports the rendered
                                 and total counts in limitations[] and pilot-summary.json, and
                                 `ripr outcome` refuses the file. Set to 0 to write every entry.
  RIPR_PILOT_PACKET_BUDGET      Maximum packets in the pilot packet file. Default: 3, with
                                 actionable packets first, so the file stays small enough to
                                 read. Set to 0 to write every packet (often 2-4 MB). When the
                                 bound cuts, limitations[] reports packets_emitted and
                                 packets_eligible. The `ripr check` packet format is unaffected
                                 and writes the full set.
  RIPR_REPO_EXPOSURE_SEAM_LIMIT Maximum gaps analyzed and ranked in one pilot run.
                                 Default: the pilot seam budget (2000), so pilot does not
                                 classify seams it would not rank; `ripr check` keeps 10000.
                                 Set to 0 to analyze every seam. When the
                                 limit cuts the ranking, the terminal and summary state
                                 the summary reports how many spots were ranked, and actionable totals become
                                 lower bounds until you raise or remove the limit.
  RIPR_GIT_TIMEOUT              Cooperative deadline in seconds for each git invocation
                                 in the current-change discovery path, exactly as `ripr
                                 check` uses it. When the deadline trips, the pilot
                                 scope line reads `current change: git timed out`
                                 (pilot keeps fixed phrases for determinism; the
                                 machine-readable git_invocation_timeout name is what
                                 `ripr check` reports). 0 disables the deadline.
                                 Invalid values are rejected. Default: 300 (5 minutes).

Outputs:
  - repo-exposure.json and repo-exposure.md
  - agent-seam-packets.json
  - pilot-summary.json and pilot-summary.md

The pilot packet is advisory. It reports saved-workspace static gap evidence
and points to one next focused test action; it does not run mutation testing,
edit source files, or configure CI policy. If analysis exceeds the timeout,
pilot-summary.json and pilot-summary.md are written with status=partial and an
explicit retry command.

Timeout exit-code contract: a timeout partial run still exits 0 — the packet,
not the exit code, is the verdict, and a stderr line discloses this at the
time it happens. CI must gate on pilot-summary.json's top-level `status`
field (`complete` vs `partial`), never on the exit code alone, or a timed-out
run reads as success.

Examples:
  ripr pilot --root .
```

### plus

`ripr help plus`

```text
Compose the repo-wide RIPR+ receipt from an existing report artifact.

Usage: ripr plus --repo-exposure-summary <path> | --gap-ledger <path> [--check]

Options:
  --repo-exposure-summary <path>  Compose the receipt from a repo-exposure-summary-json artifact (pure composition).
  --gap-ledger <path>             Compose the receipt from a gap decision ledger (ledger-only composition; no repo scan).
  --check                         Require established zero; incomplete evidence exits 2.

Exit status: 0 when the receipt was composed; 2 when the named artifact
cannot be read or composed, or --check cannot establish zero (an
`indeterminate` receipt is still written).

Outputs:
  target/ripr/reports/ripr-plus.json
  target/ripr/reports/ripr-plus.md
  target/ripr/reports/ripr-plus.last-good.json  (only after a read or compose failure)
  target/ripr/reports/ripr-plus.last-good.md    (only after a read or compose failure)

When the named artifact cannot be read or composed, the run still writes an
`indeterminate` receipt to ripr-plus.json. If an earlier run composed the
receipt it replaces (any status other than `indeterminate`, or `indeterminate`
with cause `quality_evidence_incomplete`), that receipt is first copied to
ripr-plus.last-good.json, and its Markdown beside it as
ripr-plus.last-good.md only when the canonical Markdown is that receipt's
projection; a leftover `.md` from another run is then dropped. An earlier
failed run's error receipt is never kept. A --check failure on a composed
receipt writes that receipt and makes no last-good copy; a copy an earlier
failure left stays until a later failure replaces it.
The copy describes an earlier run, may be stale for the current HEAD, and is
not current evidence.

Current inputs contain exposure or ledger evidence only. They do not establish
complete test-efficiency measurement, bind that evidence to current candidate
bytes, or dispose of blocked and unsupported scope. Known actionable counts remain informational; complete unresolved debt
and candidate authority remain indeterminate, so --check cannot pass from these
inputs. No ripr command produces the missing inputs yet, so
these receipts stay indeterminate until that lands. This command does not scan a
repository or turn raw seams into debt.

Examples:
  ripr plus --gap-ledger target/ripr/reports/gap-decision-ledger.json
```

### policy

`ripr help policy`

```text
Summarize which RIPR policy posture is safe for the current repo.

Usage: ripr policy readiness [--root PATH] [--gate-decision PATH] [--baseline-delta PATH] [--recommendation-calibration PATH] [--mutation-calibration PATH] [--waiver-aging PATH] [--suppression-health PATH] [--repo-config PATH] [--previous-readiness PATH] [--out PATH] [--out-md PATH]
       ripr policy operations [--root PATH] --policy-readiness PATH [--waiver-aging PATH] [--suppression-health PATH] [--baseline-delta PATH] [--gate-decision PATH] [--recommendation-calibration PATH] [--mutation-calibration PATH] [--preview-boundary PATH] [--out PATH] [--out-md PATH]
       ripr policy history [--root PATH] --current PATH [--history PATH] [--commit REV] [--pr-number NUMBER] [--out PATH] [--out-md PATH] [--out-jsonl PATH]
       ripr policy promote [--root PATH] --to MODE --operations PATH [--history PATH] [--out PATH] [--out-md PATH]
       ripr policy preview-promote [--root PATH] --language LANGUAGE --class CLASS [--evidence PATH] [--out PATH] [--out-md PATH]
       ripr policy waiver-aging [--root PATH] [--ledger PATH] [--history PATH] [--out PATH] [--out-md PATH]
       ripr policy suppression-health [--root PATH] [--manifest PATH] [--out PATH] [--out-md PATH]

Readiness options:
  --root PATH                           Display root for the report. Defaults to current directory.
  --gate-decision PATH                  Optional gate-decision JSON from `ripr gate evaluate`.
  --baseline-delta PATH                 Optional baseline-debt-delta JSON from `ripr baseline diff`.
  --recommendation-calibration PATH     Optional recommendation calibration JSON.
  --mutation-calibration PATH           Optional imported mutation calibration JSON.
  --waiver-aging PATH                   Optional waiver-aging JSON.
  --suppression-health PATH             Optional suppression-health JSON.
  --repo-config PATH                    Optional repo config summary JSON.
  --previous-readiness PATH             Optional prior policy-readiness JSON.
  --out PATH                            JSON output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/policy-readiness.json.
  --out-md PATH                         Markdown output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/policy-readiness.md.

Operations options:
  --root PATH                           Display root for the report. Defaults to current directory.
  --policy-readiness PATH               Policy-readiness JSON from `ripr policy readiness`.
  --waiver-aging PATH                   Optional waiver-aging JSON.
  --suppression-health PATH             Optional suppression-health JSON.
  --baseline-delta PATH                 Optional baseline-debt-delta JSON.
  --gate-decision PATH                  Optional gate-decision JSON.
  --recommendation-calibration PATH     Optional recommendation calibration JSON.
  --mutation-calibration PATH           Optional imported mutation calibration JSON.
  --preview-boundary PATH               Optional preview-boundary JSON.
  --out PATH                            JSON output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/policy-operations.json.
  --out-md PATH                         Markdown output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/policy-operations.md.

History options:
  --root PATH                           Display root for the report. Defaults to current directory.
  --current PATH                        Policy-operations JSON from `ripr policy operations`.
  --history PATH                        Optional policy history JSONL.
  --commit REV                          Optional current snapshot commit identity.
  --pr-number NUMBER                    Optional current snapshot PR number.
  --out PATH                            JSON output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/policy-history.json.
  --out-md PATH                         Markdown output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/policy-history.md.
  --out-jsonl PATH                      Optional append-only JSONL producer. Writes one compact snapshot line per run (`example_append_record`). Generated CI does not pass this flag.

Promotion options:
  --root PATH                           Display root for the report. Defaults to current directory.
  --to MODE                             Target mode: visible-only, acknowledgeable, baseline-check, or calibrated-gate.
  --operations PATH                     Policy-operations JSON from `ripr policy operations`.
  --history PATH                        Optional policy-history JSON from `ripr policy history`.
  --out PATH                            JSON output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/policy-promotion-<mode>.json.
  --out-md PATH                         Markdown output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/policy-promotion-<mode>.md.

Preview promotion options:
  --root PATH                           Display root for the report. Defaults to current directory.
  --language LANGUAGE                   Preview language under review: typescript or python.
  --class CLASS                         Preview evidence class under review, for example boundary_gap.
  --evidence PATH                       Optional explicit preview promotion evidence receipts JSON.
  --out PATH                            JSON output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/preview-promotion-<language>-<class>.json.
  --out-md PATH                         Markdown output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/preview-promotion-<language>-<class>.md.

Waiver aging options:
  --root PATH                           Display root for the report. Defaults to current directory.
  --ledger PATH                         Optional current PR evidence ledger JSON.
  --history PATH                        Optional PR evidence ledger JSONL history.
  --out PATH                            JSON output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/waiver-aging.json.
  --out-md PATH                         Markdown output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/waiver-aging.md.

Suppression health options:
  --root PATH                           Workspace root for reading the manifest. Defaults to current directory.
  --manifest PATH                       Suppression manifest path. Defaults to .ripr/suppressions.toml.
  --out PATH                            JSON output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/suppression-health.json.
  --out-md PATH                         Markdown output path. Defaults to target/ripr/reports/suppression-health.md.

The policy readiness report is read-only advisory governance over explicit
existing artifacts. It recommends advisory-only, visible-only, acknowledgeable,
baseline-check, or calibrated-gate posture without executing a gate. Preview
language evidence stays visible and advisory by default.

The policy operations report composes existing policy artifacts into current
ceiling, next safe action, safe/not-safe promotion modes, blockers, and input
health without promoting anything.

The policy history report shows whether readiness, waivers, suppressions,
baseline debt, calibration, and preview boundaries are improving or decaying
without appending history unless `--out-jsonl` is supplied.

The policy promotion packet reads policy operations plus optional policy
history and writes manual-review promotion evidence without changing config.

The preview promotion packet writes default blocked evidence accounting for
TypeScript and Python preview classes while keeping preview evidence visible,
advisory, non-gating, outside RIPR Zero, and outside calibrated confidence
until a later explicit policy is reviewed.

The waiver-aging report keeps repeated waivers visible as repair or
policy-review signals.

The suppression-health report flags durable exception metadata gaps while
keeping suppressed findings visible.

These policy commands do not run analysis, mutate baselines or suppressions,
post comments, edit source, generate tests, run mutation testing, change gate
policy, promote preview evidence, or make CI blocking.

Examples:
  ripr policy history --current target/ripr/reports/policy-operations.json
  ripr policy operations --policy-readiness target/ripr/reports/policy-readiness.json
  ripr policy preview-promote --language typescript --class boundary_gap
  ripr policy promote --to baseline-check --operations target/ripr/reports/policy-operations.json
  ripr policy readiness
  ripr policy suppression-health --root .
  ripr policy waiver-aging
```

### pr-comments

`ripr help pr-comments`

```text
Plan or publish bounded inline PR comments (off / plan / inline).

Usage: ripr pr-comments plan [--root PATH] [--pr-guidance PATH] [--existing-comments PATH] [--mode off|plan|inline] [--pull-request N] [--event-name NAME] [--head-repo OWNER/REPO] [--base-repo OWNER/REPO] [--token-available | --no-token] [--write-permission | --no-write-permission] [--max-inline-comments N] [--out PATH] [--out-md PATH]

Plan options:
  --root PATH                 Workspace root label. Defaults to current directory.
  --pr-guidance PATH          PR guidance JSON from `ripr review-comments`.
  --existing-comments PATH    Optional existing RIPR comment metadata.
  --mode MODE                 off, plan, or inline. Defaults to off.
  --pull-request N            Pull request number for inline safety checks.
  --event-name NAME           GitHub event name, usually pull_request.
  --head-repo OWNER/REPO      Pull request head repository.
  --base-repo OWNER/REPO      Pull request base repository.
  --token-available           Mark a pull-request write token as available.
  --no-token                  Mark the token as unavailable. This is the default.
  --write-permission          Mark pull-request write permission as available. This is the default.
  --no-write-permission       Mark pull-request write permission as unavailable.
  --max-inline-comments N     Maximum publishable inline comments. Defaults to 3.
  --out PATH                  JSON output path. Defaults to target/ripr/review/comment-publish-plan.json.
  --out-md PATH               Markdown output path. Defaults to target/ripr/review/comment-publish-plan.md.

The PR comments plan is a read-only advisory projection over existing
`ripr review-comments` output and optional existing-comment metadata. It emits
create/update/keep/delete/skip/blocked operations for a later explicit
publisher, but it never posts comments, calls GitHub, edits source, generates
tests, runs mutation testing, changes gate authority, or makes CI blocking by
default.

Usage: ripr pr-comments existing [--root PATH] [--raw PATH] [--out PATH]

Existing options:
  --root PATH                 Workspace root. Defaults to current directory.
  --raw PATH                  `gh api --paginate --slurp` pages of the pull request's review comments. `-` reads standard input and keeps a copy there. Defaults to target/ripr/review/existing-comments.raw.json.
  --out PATH                  Existing-comment metadata for `--existing-comments`. Defaults to target/ripr/review/existing-comments.json.

Usage: ripr pr-comments summary --pull-request N --head-sha SHA [--root PATH] [--pr-guidance PATH] [--raw PATH] [--run-url URL] [--out-dir PATH]

Summary options:
  --root PATH                 Workspace root that --out-dir is relative to. Defaults to current directory.
  --pull-request N            Pull request the summary comment belongs to.
  --head-sha SHA              Head commit the digest names.
  --pr-guidance PATH          `ripr review-comments` JSON. Defaults to target/ripr/review/comments.json.
  --raw PATH                  `gh api --paginate --slurp` pages of the pull request's conversation comments. `-` reads standard input. Without it no earlier comment is found.
  --run-url URL               https link to the workflow run, shown as the full-report link.
  --out-dir PATH              Request directory relative to --root; an earlier request is replaced; absolute paths, `..` and symlinked directories are refused. Defaults to target/ripr/review/summary.

`summary` renders one short digest of the changed-behavior findings and writes
summary.tsv (method, endpoint, payload file, message; empty when there is
nothing to post) plus summary-request.json. It updates the marked comment that
github-actions[bot] posted earlier, even when the findings are gone, and posts
nothing for a clean pull request. It does not call GitHub or read a token.

Usage: ripr pr-comments requests --pull-request N --head-sha SHA [--root PATH] [--plan PATH] [--out-dir PATH]

Requests options:
  --root PATH                 Workspace root that --out-dir is relative to. Defaults to current directory.
  --pull-request N            Pull request the review is posted on.
  --head-sha SHA              Head commit the review comments are placed on.
  --plan PATH                 Publish plan. Defaults to target/ripr/review/comment-publish-plan.json.
  --out-dir PATH              Request directory relative to --root, its earlier request files are replaced; absolute paths, `..` and symlinked directories are refused. Defaults to target/ripr/review/publish.

`existing` keeps only marked comments that github-actions[bot] posted. It
does not call GitHub or read a token.

`requests` writes one JSON payload per call and requests.tsv, one line per
call in order: method, endpoint after repos/OWNER/REPO/, payload file, and the
message to print once the call succeeds. An unsafe plan writes no requests
and prints why. It does not call GitHub or read a token; the generated
workflow's comment steps hold GH_TOKEN and run `gh api`.

Examples:
  ripr pr-comments existing --root .
  ripr pr-comments plan --pr-guidance target/ripr/review/comments.json
  ripr pr-comments requests --root . --pull-request 7 --head-sha 0123abcd
  ripr pr-comments summary --root . --pull-request 7 --head-sha 0123abcd --raw -
```
